jimothy.block:
Jimothy — one of the playable characters in Jimothy, a storybook hopper set on the rainy
streets of Seattle.

STANCE (locked — the same in every frame):
  A hunched, knock-kneed raccoon who spends most of the sheet up on his two hind legs, head
  pushed forward and long arms dangling to his knees (in umbrella his free arm hangs all the
  way down to the ground). Idle, dash-run, flee, coffee, magnet, umbrella, sit, cheer and
  splash are all on two feet; scared stands on one foot with the other leg kicked out to the
  side and his paws clutched at his chest; shield is a low squat with his arms crossed over
  his face; cheer flings one long arm high overhead. He drops onto all four limbs only for
  crouch (facing the viewer head-on) and land, splayed wide and spidery, elbows and knees
  jutting out like a daddy longlegs. Run-r and run-r2 are low, bent-knee strides on the hind
  legs with one forepaw reaching ahead and never touching the ground. Run-l is an airborne
  bound: body tipped forward, both arms hanging bent at his sides, both legs trailing below
  him. Eat is the only frame where he sits on his rump, legs splayed forward. Sit shows him
  standing upright, one paw on his chest and the other on his hip. Leap is airborne with
  both arms flung straight up and the legs dangling apart; dizzy is an airborne sprawl with
  all four limbs flung out; ko lies sprawled on his back with one foot kicked up in the air
  and one paw flopped over the top of his body. Facing as drawn: run-l, dash-run, flee and
  cheer point his snout to the right; run-r, run-r2, coffee and land point it to the left.

WARDROBE AND PROPS (locked — these appear in ALL frames, including the deaths):
  Nothing. He wears no clothing, hat, collar or bag in any frame, just bare grizzled fur,
  and no prop is always present. Per-frame props, and nothing else ever: a takeaway coffee
  cup (cream paper, kraft-brown sleeve, white lid, a thin pink steam squiggle rising off it)
  held out ahead of him in coffee, with an orange spark-and-flame trail at his feet and a
  pink smoke ribbon streaming behind; an open pale kraft-cardboard takeaway box heaped with
  golden fried chunks hugged to his belly in magnet, while a glowing yellow-green arc wrapped
  in a rose-pink haze carries five gold coins (each with a small stamped mark as texture, one
  seen edge-on) toward his free paw; a dark navy umbrella (many panels, small brass tip, tiny
  brass dots at the rib ends, thin brass shaft, a grey crook handle with a green sheen
  hanging below his fist) held up in umbrella with lilac-blue rain falling around it; a
  translucent blue-violet bubble dome with white rain streaks over him in shield; the same
  kraft box tipped over on the ground in eat, spilling golden chunks and orange fries, with
  a single fry held up in his paw. Effects only: pale pink and gold speed streaks behind and
  under dash-run; red and orange streaks plus three red-orange exclamation ticks over his
  head in flee; three small peach-orange alarm ticks by his head in scared; three yellow
  stars trailing thin pink orbit dashes in dizzy and three yellow stars in ko; a blue-violet
  water crown with flying droplets in splash, where his fur is soaked into wet spikes beaded
  with water.

HOW THIS BODY WORKS:
  The silhouette is the joke: a round, egg-shaped fuzzy torso with no visible neck, the head
  perched right on top, and four very long, very skinny stick limbs with knobbly knees and
  elbows, so he reads as a furry ball on stilts. His fur is grizzled grey-brown with a dusty
  mauve cast, paler on the belly; the crown and back run warmer olive-gold in idle. Face: a
  black bandit mask wrapping both eyes, a bright cream-white brow stripe above it, a cream
  muzzle (warmer tan in magnet, umbrella and cheer), a black button nose and long white
  whiskers, with upright triangular ears that have rounded tips, pale cream rims and dark
  insides. His default eyes are huge round cream-white eyeballs with small black pupils, a
  startled stare he keeps through idle, leap, land, run-l, run-r, dash-run, flee, coffee,
  magnet, scared, cheer and splash. A few frames change them: a flat, narrowed glare in
  crouch, squeezed shut in shield, sleepy smug half-lids in sit and eat, yellow irises in
  umbrella and run-r2, and white target spirals in dizzy and ko. Hands and feet are dark
  charcoal, long and spidery, with thin fingers and long toes, set flat on the ground. The
  tail is thick and bushy, about as long as his torso, banded black-brown and tan-cream,
  usually with a dark tip; it curls round his side at rest, hangs down behind his legs in
  sit, streams straight back in run-r, run-r2, coffee and flee, wraps round under him in ko,
  and is hidden completely in run-l and dash-run. Thin orange or red rim-light edges (land,
  run-r, coffee, sit, cheer) are lighting, not fur colour. His torso size, head size and limb
  length match idle in every frame: never give him a neck, never thicken the limbs, never
  shrink the tail.
corrections: Run-l removed from the on-two-feet list: it is an airborne bound with the body tipped forward, both arms hanging bent at his sides and the legs trailing. The claim 'both arms flung out' did not match.
Scared: he stands on one foot with the other leg kicked out and his paws at his chest. The block had only listed it as on two feet.
Leap: the arms are flung straight up and the legs dangle. It is not an all-four-limbs sprawl; only dizzy is.
Ko: one foot is kicked up and one paw is flopped over his body. The claim 'feet in the air' (both) was not supported.
Facing list: added cheer (snout right) and land (snout left), and noted that crouch faces the viewer head-on.

Eyes: removed 'he keeps that startled stare' for every mood. Crouch is a narrowed glare, shield is squeezed shut, and sit and eat are sleepy half-lids. Yellow irises also appear in run-r2, not only umbrella. The ko eyes read as target spirals.

Tail: it is hidden entirely in run-l and dash-run and hangs behind his legs in sit. It streams back in run-r, run-r2, coffee and flee, so 'streams straight back in the runs' was wrong. The dark tip is usual, not guaranteed.
Ears: they are upright triangles with rounded tips, pale cream rims and dark insides, not simply 'rounded ears'.
Muzzle: noted that it runs warmer tan in magnet, umbrella and cheer.

Umbrella: the crook handle is grey with a green sheen (it was 'dark'), the shaft is thin brass, the rib ends carry tiny brass dots and the rain is lilac-blue. His free arm dangles to the ground in this frame.
Magnet: the arc is yellow-green inside a rose-pink haze. The coins carry a small stamped mark (described as texture), and one coin is edge-on. The box is pale kraft.
Shield: the bubble has white rain streaks on it.
Scared alarm ticks: there are three and they are peach-orange, not red.
Dash-run streaks are pale pink and gold, behind and under him. Dizzy stars trail pink orbit dashes.
Eat: the box spills golden chunks as well as orange fries.
Coffee added to the rim-light frames (orange edge along his back).
unsure: Run-l shows his snout pointing right while run-r and run-r2 point left, the reverse of their names; described as drawn, did not check how the game flips these frames.
The frame labelled sit shows him standing upright, not sitting.
The number of dark tail rings changes from frame to frame (roughly four to six).
A faint olive-green tint on the fingers in umbrella, sit, run-l and run-r2 looks like colour fringing, not a glove or prop.
His fur is warmer olive-gold in idle than elsewhere; unclear which tone is intended.
The golden chunks in the magnet and eat box may be fried chicken or something else; described only as golden fried chunks.
In ko one eye is a clear spiral and the other reads more like a white concentric target ring; both described as target spirals.
In run-l the eyes look faintly cream-yellow; only umbrella and run-r2 are listed as clearly yellow.
draftUnsure: run-l shows his snout pointing right while run-r and run-r2 point left, the reverse of their names; I described the facing as drawn and did not check how the game flips these frames.
The frame labelled sit shows him standing upright with a paw on his chest and a paw on his hip, not sitting.
The number of dark tail rings changes from frame to frame (roughly four to six).
A faint olive-green tint on the dangling fingers in umbrella and on the hip paw in sit looks like colour fringing, not a prop, but I cannot be certain.
His fur is noticeably warmer and more olive-gold in idle than in the other frames; I could not tell which tone is the intended one.
The golden chunks in the magnet box may be fried chicken or something else; I described them only as golden fried chunks.

shark.block:
Sharkothy — one of the playable characters in Jimothy, a storybook hopper set on the rainy
streets of Seattle.

STANCE (locked — the same in every frame):
  A plump little raccoon in a shark onesie, standing upright on his hind legs, pear-shaped
  and bottom-heavy. He is on two feet in idle, run-l, run-r, coffee, magnet, umbrella,
  scared and cheer; the side runs are upright, arm-pumping jogs with a fist leading and both
  feet off the ground mid-stride (run-l faces left, run-r faces right). Magnet and cheer
  throw both arms straight up; umbrella rests the free paw on his hip; scared clutches both
  fists under his chin. He drops onto all four paws only in crouch (a low stalk facing left)
  and land (paws slapping down into a splash). Leap is an airborne sprawl with both arms
  flung wide and both legs kicked forward, soles to the viewer. Dash-run is a flat,
  horizontal torpedo glide to the right, arms swept back and feet trailing. Flee is a low
  scramble to the left, nearly on all fours, one paw clamped on top of the hood. He sits on
  his rump in sit (hunched forward, paws clasped together at his belly) and eat (legs
  forward, soles showing), and huddles in a low squat inside the bubble in shield. Dizzy is
  a belly flop with his face turned toward the viewer; ko lies on his back with both feet
  kicked up; splash is upright in the water with both arms up.

WARDROBE AND PROPS (locked — these appear in ALL frames, including the deaths):
  ALL 19 FRAMES: one full-body shark onesie in dusty denim-blue fleece with a soft, fuzzy
  nap. The hood is the shark's head: his face peeks out of the open jaws, which are rimmed
  in cream fabric and lined with a ring of stiff white triangular felt teeth top and bottom;
  two round glossy black shark eyes sit high on either side of the hood, with a few faint
  curved gill-seam lines beside the opening. A tall curved dorsal fin rides the back,
  smaller fins stick out at his sides (they flare out on both flanks in scared), and a
  crescent shark tail fin sticks out low behind him. That tail fin is his only tail: no
  ringed raccoon tail shows in any frame. The front is a cream belly panel from chin to
  crotch with a single silver zipper down its centre, pull tab at the top. Sleeves and legs
  end in gathered cuffs, and his bare dark charcoal raccoon paws and feet come out of them.
  Per-frame props, and nothing else ever: a takeaway coffee cup (cream paper, a brown sleeve
  carrying a small plain pale oval as texture, never a logo, and a white lid) held in both
  paws just under his chin in coffee, with a grey-white steam wisp that turns into a pink
  zigzag, a few tiny orange sparks around him and small orange flames at his feet; a whirl
  of gold coins with crimped bottle-cap edges and small gold bars, laced with rose-pink and
  gold speed streaks, circling him in magnet, with two coins caught on the hood's upper
  teeth; a dark navy umbrella with a black crook handle, water dripping from every rib end,
  held up in his right paw in umbrella; in shield, a violet bubble with a honeycomb sheen,
  white crackling starbursts and a ring of blue-white splash at its base, and inside it he
  clutches a broken, inside-out black umbrella by its crook; a red fries carton full of
  golden fries held against his belly in eat, with one fry in his other paw at his mouth and
  a second fry snagged on the hood's upper teeth; a single gold bottle-cap coin under his paw
  in dizzy. Effects only: blue-white spray with a violet tint under land and dash-run, water
  spray behind flee plus two yellow-orange exclamation ticks, yellow four-point sparkles and
  a couple of falling drops in cheer, four yellow stars in dizzy and three in ko, and a
  blue-white water crown with violet tints in splash, where the whole costume is soaked dark
  and dripping.

HOW THIS BODY WORKS:
  The costume fills him out into a soft, chubby pear with short stubby limbs and a big
  hooded head; no skinny raccoon limbs show anywhere. Only three bits of raccoon are ever
  visible: the face in the jaws, and the charcoal paws and feet at the cuffs. The face is a
  proper raccoon: black bandit mask, cream-white brows, tawny brown cheek fur, a black nose,
  long white whiskers poking out past the felt teeth, and big round white eyes with black
  pupils (half-lidded and smug in umbrella and sit, half-lidded and rolled sideways in eat,
  huge in coffee, scared, shield and splash, white spirals with the tongue lolling out in
  dizzy, glazed with the tongue lolling out in ko). The joke is that the teeth frame his face
  as if he is being eaten, and in idle, umbrella and sit he could not be less bothered. The
  hood never turns into a real shark head, never closes over his face, and the teeth are
  always soft white felt, never real and never bloody. The hood's two black eyes stay high
  on the sides, the zipper stays one silver line down the cream panel, and the blue stays
  the same dusty denim in every dry frame; splash is the only frame where it goes dark and
  wet.
corrections: Leap: both legs are kicked forward with the soles to the viewer. The feet are not tucked.
Sit: he is hunched forward with his paws clasped together at his belly, not folded in his lap.
Dizzy: he lies on his belly but his face is turned toward the viewer. It is not face-down.

Coffee cup: the cup is cream with a brown sleeve and a small pale oval on the sleeve. The block had a brown cup with a cream band and a dark oval. He holds it just under his chin. The steam starts grey-white and turns into a pink zigzag, and tiny orange sparks float around him.
Umbrella: the crook handle is black and water drips from every rib end.
Shield: added the ring of blue-white splash at the base of the bubble.
Eat: added a second fry snagged on the hood's upper teeth, and noted that the carton is held against his belly.
Effects: land, dash-run and splash spray carry violet tints. The cheer sparkles are four-point.
Stance: noted that the side runs have both feet off the ground, magnet and cheer throw both arms up, umbrella rests a paw on his hip, and scared clutches both fists under his chin.
Eyes: removed 'wet' from scared, since the eyes are huge but not visibly wet. Added eat (half-lidded, rolled sideways), huge eyes in coffee and shield, and the lolling tongue in dizzy and ko.
'He could not be less bothered' now applies only to idle, umbrella and sit. Flee, scared, shield and splash show him very bothered.
'Gathered elastic cuffs' became 'gathered cuffs'. The leg cuffs are gathered, but elastic is not readable.
unsure: The number and placement of the smaller side fins changes between frames; clearest in scared.
The gill-seam lines are faint and not equally visible in every frame.
In coffee a small orange-gold bit sits in his mouth beside the cup (a crumb, a fry or a steam artefact); not described.
The gold objects in magnet and dizzy have crimped edges like bottle caps; unclear whether meant as coins or caps.
In shield he holds a broken, inside-out umbrella; unclear whether intended or a generation accident.
In dash-run a little dark raccoon leg seems to show above the trailing feet; may be shading.
draftUnsure: The number and placement of the smaller side fins changes between frames; they are clearest in scared, where they stick out on both flanks.
The faint gill-seam lines are only clearly visible in some frames (idle, dizzy), so they may not be a fixed feature.
The small dark oval on the coffee cup band could be meant as a logo shape; I described it only as plain texture.
The gold objects in magnet and dizzy have crimped edges like bottle caps; I could not tell whether they are meant as coins or caps.
In shield he holds a broken, inside-out umbrella; I could not tell whether that is intended or a generation accident.

froggery.block:
Froggothy — one of the playable characters in Jimothy, a storybook hopper set on the rainy
streets of Seattle.

STANCE (locked — the same in every frame):
  A small, round-bellied raccoon in a frog suit, upright on his hind legs for most of the
  sheet: idle (one glove on his hip), run-l, run-r, dash-run, flee, coffee, magnet (both
  arms flung up and out), umbrella (free glove on his belly), scared (hunched, both gloves
  clutching the tongue curl at his chest), cheer (one knee kicked up, arms up and out) and
  splash (both arms up). He goes frog-low only when a move calls for it: crouch is a
  splay-legged frog squat on all four limbs facing right, land is a wide squat on both
  flippers with arms flung out to the sides, and shield is a deep sumo squat with both palms
  pushed forward. Leap is an airborne frog kick with knees up and one arm waving high. The
  side runs are upright jogging strides with fists pumping (run-l faces left, run-r faces
  right); dash-run sprints to the right, and flee scrambles to the left with one glove
  clamped on his hood. He sits on his rump in sit (gloves folded on his belly) and eat. Dizzy
  is a belly flop with his face turned to the viewer; ko lies on his back with both flipper
  feet kicked high.

WARDROBE AND PROPS (locked — these appear in ALL frames, including the deaths):
  ALL 19 FRAMES: one bright leaf-green frog onesie with a slightly glossy, rubbery sheen,
  dotted all over with darker green round spots. The hood is the frog's head: two big
  bulging frog eyes sit on top (cream-white with black pupils, set in green lids), two small
  dark nostril dimples sit between them, the face opening is trimmed in pale yellow-green
  piping, and a row of darker green crest bumps runs from the crown down the back of the
  hood and along the spine (rounded in most frames, sharpened into pointed spikes in flee,
  shield and ko). A pale yellow-green oval belly panel with a stitched centre seam covers the
  front. His hands are green frog gloves with splayed fingers and round fingertip pads, and
  his feet are long green webbed flippers with round toe pads. At his throat hangs a red felt
  frog tongue rolled into a tight spiral like a rosette, and it changes shape by frame: in
  dash-run it reads as a flat red neckerchief; in flee it hangs half-unrolled at his throat
  while a separate long red ribbon streams back from his neck; in magnet, cheer and splash it
  hangs unrolled from just under his chin as a long red strip ending in the curl (in magnet a
  golden fry is poked through the curl); in dizzy and ko the curl sits right at his mouth
  beside his lolling tongue. His own ringed raccoon tail, grey-cream and black, sticks out of
  the seat of the suit in nearly every frame (hidden in land and coffee). The glove wrists
  end in a flared or spiky green cuff, and pale yellow-green scalloped frills ring the wrists
  and ankles in flee, magnet, umbrella, shield, scared, cheer, dizzy, splash and ko.
  Per-frame props, and nothing else ever: a takeaway coffee cup (cream paper, kraft-brown
  sleeve, dark brown lid) held in both gloves in coffee, with jittery pink squiggles all
  around him, a grey-white steam wisp curling up into pink, and orange flames licking at his
  feet; a spray of gold crimped-edge coins and golden fry sticks flying round him in magnet,
  with one red-centred gold cap perched on top of his hood between the frog eyes; a black
  umbrella with a crook handle, dripping lilac drops, held in his right glove in umbrella; a
  violet bubble with white vein cracks in shield, where the hood's frog eyes glow white; a
  kraft-brown paper bag of fries hugged in one glove in eat, with a single fry held to his
  mouth by the other. Effects only: blue-white splash with a violet tint under land, pale
  speed streaks and a pale spray at his feet in dash-run, red and green speed streaks behind
  flee, pink and violet four-point sparkles in cheer, three yellow stars on an orbit line in
  dizzy and ko, and a blue-white splash in splash, where the suit is soaked, glossy and
  dripping.

HOW THIS BODY WORKS:
  Under the suit he is a small, soft, pear-shaped raccoon with short sturdy limbs; the suit
  rounds his shoulders and puffs his belly, and the long webbed flippers give every step its
  slap. Only his face and tail are raccoon: grey-brown fur, a black bandit mask, pale cream
  brow marks, a white muzzle, a black nose and white whiskers. His own eyes sit inside the
  mask and change with the mood (sleepy half-lids in idle, sit and umbrella; a narrowed side
  glance in crouch and the side runs; wide white eyes in leap, land, dash-run and coffee;
  wide yellow eyes in flee, magnet, scared, cheer and splash; happily squeezed shut in eat; a
  gritted squint in shield; cream spiral eyes in dizzy; one shut and one crossed out in ko).
  Meanwhile the hood's two frog eyes stay on top of his head and do their own acting: one
  winks in leap and eat, one droops half-lidded in umbrella, they bulge and pop sideways in
  scared, dizzy and ko, and they glow white in shield. The frog eyes are always two, always
  perched high on the hood and always bigger than his own, and that two-eyes-on-the-hood
  silhouette is the read at a glance. The hands are always green frog gloves, never raccoon
  paws; the feet are always webbed flippers, never raccoon feet; the red tongue curl always
  hangs at his throat. The family trade is crossing roads, so he always looks slightly ready
  to hop.
corrections: Coffee cup: the lid is dark brown, not white. The cup is cream with a kraft-brown sleeve. The steam is a grey-white wisp that turns pink.
Flee: the tongue curl still hangs half-unrolled at his throat, and a separate long red ribbon streams back from his neck. The block had the tongue itself becoming the ribbon.
The tongue hangs unrolled from under his chin in magnet and cheer too, not only in splash. In dizzy and ko the curl sits at his mouth beside a lolling tongue.
Frills: added splash. In the frames without frills (idle, coffee, the runs), the glove wrists end in a flared or spiky green cuff.
Crest: the bumps become pointed spikes in flee, shield and ko. 'Rounded' is not true in every frame.
Added two small dark nostril dimples on the hood between the frog eyes (clear in idle and coffee).
Frog eyes: they are cream-white. Added more of their acting: one winks in leap and eat, and one droops in umbrella.

His own eyes: cheer added to the yellow list. Crouch and the runs are a narrowed side glance. Leap, land, dash-run and coffee are wide white. Eat is happily squeezed shut and shield is a gritted squint. The dizzy spirals are cream with dark lines, not white.
Stance: added magnet (arms up and out), umbrella (glove on belly), scared (gloves clutching the tongue curl) and splash (arms up). Dizzy is a belly flop with his face turned to the viewer.
Effects: the land splash has a violet tint, and dash-run has a pale spray at his feet.
Eat: the bag is kraft-brown paper held in one glove, and the fry is held to his mouth by the other.
unsure: Whether the dash-run neckerchief and the flee ribbon are the tongue piece or separate garments.
Whether the scalloped wrist and ankle frills are meant to be permanent; they appear only in the listed frames.
The ringed tail is not visible in land or coffee.
The flying items in magnet read as gold bottle-cap coins and golden fries; intended item unconfirmed.
Glove finger count is inconsistent (four in some frames, five in others), so left unstated.
In magnet, cheer and splash the unrolled red strip starts right under his open mouth and could be read as his own tongue; described as hanging from under his chin.
draftUnsure: I read the red spiral at the throat as a rolled felt frog tongue; in dash-run and flee it looks more like a red neckerchief or ribbon, so it may be two different pieces.
The scalloped wrist and ankle frills appear in some frames and not others; I could not tell whether they are meant to be permanent.
The ringed tail is not visible in land or coffee.
The flying items in magnet read as gold bottle-cap coins and golden fries; I could not confirm the intended item.
The glove finger count is not consistent between frames (it looks like four in some and five in others), so I left it unstated.

dino.block:
Dinothy — one of the playable characters in Jimothy, a storybook hopper set on the rainy
streets of Seattle.

STANCE (locked — the same in every frame):
  A squat, bottom-heavy raccoon in an inflatable dinosaur suit, upright on his hind legs,
  with the suit's long tail resting on the ground behind him like a kickstand. He stands
  upright in idle (one paw on his hip), coffee, magnet (both arms thrown up), umbrella (free
  paw on his belly), scared (paws at his chest), cheer (both arms thrown up, tail lifted high
  behind) and splash (arms up). Crouch is a low, heavy stoop facing right, one bare paw
  planted on the ground, a little green claw reaching forward and the tail curled behind;
  land is a wide squat on both feet in a splash, both short arms bent in front of him. Leap is
  airborne with knees up, both soles to the viewer and both arms thrown up. The side runs are
  upright, heavy, trundling jogs with fists pumping (run-l faces left, run-r faces right) and
  the tail curving up and out behind. Dash-run charges to the right; flee runs to the left
  with one paw clapped on the hood. Sit and eat sit on his rump with legs out and dark soles
  showing. Shield is a hunched squat with both paws at his cheeks. Dizzy is a belly flop with
  his face toward the viewer and his body curling away behind him; ko lies on his back, soles
  up.

WARDROBE AND PROPS (locked — these appear in ALL frames, including the deaths):
  ALL 19 FRAMES: one glossy lime-green inflatable dinosaur suit, puffed and quilted into fat
  padded segments with a plastic sheen and bright highlights. The hood is a big, blunt
  dinosaur head: his face looks out from under the upper jaw, which overhangs like a visor
  and carries a row of cream triangular teeth, with a few smaller teeth along the lower edge
  of the opening; two round nostril holes sit at the snout tip, and one round cream eye with
  a black pupil sits high on each side under a bumpy brow. Dark green tiger stripes run over
  the hood, down the back and across the long, thick, tapering tail. The front is a
  mustard-yellow belly panel ridged into horizontal segments like a crocodile's belly, with a
  faint seam down its centre. Tiny green dinosaur arms with little clawed green hands stick
  out from the upper chest and flanks, separate from his real arms, in idle, crouch, the side
  runs, dash-run, scared, sit and eat. A small dark olive-green ribbed pack sits on his back
  between the shoulders; it shows in almost every frame where his back or side is visible
  (crouch, leap, land, the runs, dash-run, flee, coffee, magnet, umbrella, shield, scared,
  sit, eat, cheer), and the tiny red tag on it is clearest in crouch. His own bare dark
  charcoal raccoon paws come out of the sleeves in most frames, but in leap and land both
  sleeves end in little green clawed hands instead and no dark paw shows. His own dark raccoon
  feet, with pale claws and black sole pads, come out of the legs in every frame. Per-frame
  props, and nothing else ever: a takeaway coffee cup (cream paper, kraft-brown sleeve, dark
  lid) held in both paws in coffee, with black and white jitter squiggles, a pink steam curl
  and orange flames at his feet; a ring of gold coins (each stamped with a small plain mark as
  texture) and gold bars, trailing thin pink-gold orbit lines, whirling round his middle in
  magnet; a black umbrella with a crook handle held up in his left paw in umbrella, dripping;
  a violet honeycomb bubble with a white-violet crackle at its rim in shield; a red fries
  carton full of golden fries in eat, with one fry in his paw at his mouth and one caught on a
  hood tooth. Effects only: a small white splash under land (its puddles must read clear
  blue-white, never magenta), a pale green and pink speed smear under his heels plus faint
  pink streaks behind dash-run, red lightning ticks over his head and at his heels plus pink
  streaks in flee, gold four-point sparkles in cheer, a ring of yellow stars on an orbit line
  in dizzy, three yellow stars in ko, and a blue-white water crown in splash, where the suit
  is soaked darker.

HOW THIS BODY WORKS:
  The suit turns him into a fat green pear: short thick legs, a big round belly, a tall head
  and a long thick tail, so his weight sits low and every pose should feel heavy and bouncy,
  like a pool toy. Only three bits of raccoon show: the face under the jaw, the dark paws at
  the sleeve ends (except in leap and land) and the dark feet at the leg ends. The face: grey
  fur, a black bandit mask, cream-white brows, a white muzzle, a black nose and white
  whiskers. His eyes sit inside the mask and run from sleepy, smug half-lids (idle, crouch,
  umbrella, sit, eat) to wide round white eyes, grinning in leap, land and the side runs and
  panicked in dash-run, flee, coffee, scared, shield and splash, to white target spirals with
  a lolling tongue (dizzy) and rolled-up half-lids with the tongue out (ko). The suit's own
  cream eyes and teeth never move or act. Wherever the tiny chest arms appear they stay tiny
  and sit on the chest, separate from his real arms. There is no raccoon tail anywhere; the
  striped dino tail is the only tail. The green stays one glossy lime in every dry frame, the
  belly stays mustard, and the teeth stay soft-looking cream triangles, never sharp white and
  never bloody. Extinct, allegedly; he has never looked more pleased with himself.
corrections: Paws: in leap and land both arms end in little green clawed hands and no dark raccoon paw shows. 'His own bare dark paws come out of the sleeves' was not true in every frame.

Chest arms: they are not always present. They show in idle, crouch, the side runs, dash-run, scared, sit and eat, and they sometimes sit on the flanks as well as the chest. 'Always there' was removed.
The claw hands are no longer called three-clawed, because the finger count varies. They are now 'little clawed green hands'.
Pack: it is also visible in leap, land and cheer, which the writer said it was not, and faintly in coffee. It reads as a dark olive ribbed lump, and the red tag is clearest in crouch.
Coffee cup: the lid is dark, not white. The cup is cream with a kraft sleeve. The jitter squiggles are black and white.
Land splash: the reference puddles are magenta-tinted. They are rewritten as a white splash that must read blue-white, and magenta is forbidden.
Dash-run: the smear sits under his heels (pale green and pink), with faint pink streaks behind. Flee: red lightning ticks also appear at his heels.
Magnet: added the thin pink-gold orbit lines.
Shield: his paws are at his cheeks, and the bubble rim has a white-violet crackle.
Eyes: leap, land and the side runs are wide and grinning, not panic eyes. Coffee, dash-run and shield are panicked. Added ko (rolled half-lids, tongue out) and the dizzy tongue.
Added the faint vertical centre seam on the belly panel.
Stance: land has short arms bent in front, cheer lifts the tail high, crouch has a green claw reaching forward, and dizzy has his face toward the viewer.
unsure: The pack could be the suit's inflation fan housing or a small backpack; it looks boxy in crouch and round in leap and land.
In idle, the green claw arm on his right side could be his real right arm in a claw sleeve or a second tiny chest arm.
In leap and land it is unclear whether the green-clawed arms are his real arms in claw sleeves or the tiny arms drawn larger.
The small stamped mark on the magnet coins is too small to read; described only as a plain mark.
The pack is not visible in idle, dizzy or splash, and only as a small lump in ko.
In dizzy the green shape curling behind him is probably the tail but is hard to separate from his legs.
The back edge of the hood in coffee picks up a purple tint that looks like a colour leak; not described.
draftUnsure: The small olive-green boxy pack on his back (with a tiny red tag) could be the suit's inflation fan or a little backpack; I could not tell which.
Two tiny chest arms are clear in most frames, but in idle one of them could be read as his real left arm in a green claw sleeve.
I could not confirm whether the lower edge of the hood opening has a full row of teeth or only a few.
The small stamped mark on the magnet coins is too small to read; I described it only as a plain mark.
The pack is hard to see in coffee and not visible in idle, leap, land or cheer.

knight.block:
Cardboard Knight Jimothy — one of the playable characters in Jimothy, a storybook hopper set
on the rainy streets of Seattle.

STANCE (locked — the same in every frame):
  A short, stocky raccoon standing upright on his hind legs in most frames, feet planted wide
  like a very small, very brave guard. Idle holds his wooden spoon up like a sword, shield on
  his other arm. Crouch is a low fencer's crouch, shield forward and spoon held low and back.
  Leap is airborne, knees up, spoon raised. Land is a wide squat in a splash with the spoon
  still up. The side runs are airborne charging strides with the torn cape streaming behind,
  shield leading and spoon trailing (run-l faces left, run-r faces right); dash-run charges to
  the right with the spoon held low across his body, and flee runs to the left with one paw
  clapped on his helmet and the spoon held low in front. Coffee, magnet, umbrella and cheer
  are all upright on two feet. Scared is a startled backward hop, knees bent, boots kicked out
  in front and spoon still raised. Shield is a braced, low guard crouch behind the shield with
  the spoon thrust out. Sit and eat sit cross-legged on the ground with the spoon across his
  lap and the shield leaning at his side. Dizzy is a face-down belly flop with the shield on
  his back; ko lies on his back with one boot up; splash is upright in the water with the
  spoon held high.

WARDROBE AND PROPS (locked — these appear in ALL frames, including the deaths):
  ALL 19 FRAMES: a full suit of armour made from brown kraft cardboard, rain-spotted, with
  corrugated edges showing, patched and held together with strips of silver-grey duct tape.
  The helmet is a boxy cardboard box pulled over his head with the front cut away to frame
  his face; his two furry grey-and-black ears poke out at its top corners, and tape covers its
  corners and seams. The body armour is a boxy cardboard breastplate with tape bands, flat
  cardboard shoulder plates and short cardboard tassets over the hips; across the collar runs
  a grey tape strap with one round red jewel at its centre. His forearms show his own dark
  grey fur wrapped in tape bands, his thighs show bare dark grey fur between the tassets and
  the boots, his hands wear tan cardboard mitten gauntlets, and his feet are in chunky, tall
  cardboard box boots with tape strips and cross-stitched seams across the toes and soles. A
  tattered red cape hangs from his shoulders, torn into ragged strips, and often shows only as
  flying red shreds. Two props appear in every single frame. The first is a big honey-brown
  wooden kitchen spoon, his sword, held in his right paw; it moves to his left paw, held
  across his belly, in umbrella, is tucked under his right arm with the bowl poking out in
  coffee, lies across his lap in sit and eat, lies dropped by his paw in dizzy, and is still
  gripped in one paw in ko. The second is a round cardboard shield with a rolled rim and a big
  X of grey duct tape across its face, worn on his left arm; it leans at his side in sit and
  eat, rides on his back in dizzy and lies on his chest in ko, and run-l is drawn as a mirror
  of run-r, so shield and spoon swap sides there. Per-frame props, and nothing else ever: a
  plain cream paper cup with no lid held in both paws in coffee, with pink steam curls, orange
  flames at his feet and bloodshot, red-rimmed eyes; a swirl of gold coins and gold bars with
  thin red orbit lines round him in magnet; a charcoal-grey umbrella with a thin straight
  shaft and a crook handle held up in his right paw in umbrella; a violet honeycomb bubble
  with white crackling edges in shield; a red fries carton full of golden fries in eat, with
  one fry at his mouth (the carton carries only a plain yellow rounded outline as texture,
  never a brand logo). Effects only: a white splash under land (its puddle must read clear
  blue-white, never magenta), red and orange speed streaks plus flying tape scraps in
  dash-run and flee, blue sweat drops in scared, gold sparkles and a few coins in cheer,
  three yellow stars on an orbit line in dizzy, three yellow stars in ko, and a blue-white
  water crown in splash, where the cardboard is soaked dark.

HOW THIS BODY WORKS:
  He is a small, stocky, chibi-proportioned raccoon: a big boxed head roughly a third of his
  height, a compact square torso, short thick limbs, and a ringed dark-grey-and-cream bushy
  tail poking out behind the armour in many frames (idle, crouch, leap, land, dash-run,
  coffee, shield, scared, eat, cheer, dizzy). The box helmet and square breastplate make him
  read as a little stack of boxes at a glance, and that blocky outline must never soften into
  real armour: every plate is flat brown cardboard and duct tape, never steel and never
  painted silver. His face inside the box is the only fur-forward part: grey fur, a black
  bandit mask, cream-white brows, a white muzzle, a black nose, and large glossy amber-brown
  eyes with bright highlights. The eyebrows do the acting: stern and heroic in idle, crouch
  and land; grinning in leap and the side runs; worried in scared and eat; heavy-lidded and
  unimpressed in umbrella and sit; a squint in shield and a gleeful squint in cheer; wide and
  glassy in splash; spirals in dizzy; half-shut with the tongue out in ko. The spoon is always
  a plain wooden spoon, never a real sword, and the shield is always round cardboard with the
  tape X, never a painted crest. The armour came out of a fridge box and stays shabby in
  every frame; all the valour is in the pose.
corrections: Scared: this is a startled backward hop with knees bent and boots kicked out in front, not upright on two feet. It was removed from the upright list, and the phrase 'every frame except the falls' became 'most frames'.
Side runs: both feet are off the ground, the shield leads and the spoon trails.
Flee: the spoon is held low in front in his free paw, visible below the shield. This partly answers the writer's doubt.
Shins: they are covered by the tall cardboard boots. The bare dark grey fur shows at the thighs, so 'shins wrapped in tape bands' was not supported. The forearm tape over fur is kept.
Boots: the cross-stitching runs across the toes and soles (clearest in sit and eat).
Shield: noted that it leans at his side in sit and eat and rides on his back in dizzy, since 'worn on his left arm' is not true there.
Umbrella: the spoon is held across his belly in his left paw, and the umbrella shaft is thin.
Fries carton: it carries a yellow rounded outline shape, not a band. It is described as texture and never a logo.
Land splash: the reference puddle is magenta-tinted. It is rewritten as a white splash that must read blue-white, with magenta forbidden.
Tail: the vague 'most frames' became an explicit list of the frames where the tail is visible. Its colour is dark grey and cream, not grey and black.
Helmet: it is boxy and slightly angular, not strictly square. The ears poke out at the top corners.
Expressions: added grinning in leap and the runs, worried in eat, a squint in shield and cheer, spirals in dizzy, and half-shut eyes with the tongue out in ko.
Dizzy: three stars. Ko: one boot up, not both.
unsure: In run-l and run-r the shield and spoon swap sides as mirrors; unclear which paw is meant to hold the spoon in each.
Whether the forearm wraps are tape over bare fur or grey sleeves.
The gauntlets read as tan cardboard mittens in most frames but look browner and more glove-like in eat.
The round red collar jewel could be meant as a bottle cap or a button.
The yellow rounded outline on the fries carton resembles a fast-food emblem; described as plain texture and must stay unbranded.
The cape's length and condition change a lot; in several frames it is only loose red shreds.
In sit a small grey object pokes out under the shield; could be the tail tip or debris, not listed.
draftUnsure: run-l is drawn as a mirror of run-r, so the spoon and shield swap sides there; in flee I could not tell which paw holds the spoon.
I could not tell whether the forearm and shin wraps are tape over bare fur or grey sleeves.
The gauntlets read as tan cardboard mittens in most frames but look browner and more glove-like in eat.
The round red collar jewel could be meant as a bottle cap or a button.
The fries carton in eat has a yellow emblem shape that resembles a fast-food logo; I described it as a plain band and it should stay unbranded.
The cape's length and condition change a lot; in several frames it is only loose red shreds.

hazmat.block:
Hazmat Jimothy — one of the playable characters in Jimothy, a storybook hopper set on the
rainy streets of Seattle.

STANCE (locked — the same in every frame):
  A chunky raccoon in a puffy suit, upright on his hind legs in heavy boots, a little stiff
  and waddly because of the suit. He is upright in idle (one gloved hand on his hip), run-l,
  run-r, dash-run, flee, coffee, magnet (both arms up), umbrella (free glove on his belly),
  scared (hunched, both gloves up at the respirator), cheer (both arms up, one knee kicked
  high) and splash (arms up, one boot kicked). Crouch is a sprinter's crouch facing right, one
  glove planted on the ground and the other reaching forward. Leap is airborne with knees
  tucked and one arm waving up. Land is a wide squat in a splash with one glove on the ground.
  The side runs are upright, arm-pumping strides with the loose air hose flapping behind
  (run-l faces left, run-r faces right); dash-run and flee both run to the right, flee with
  one glove clapped to the hood. Shield is a deep squat with both palms pushed out. Sit and
  eat sit on his rump with legs out and boot soles to the viewer. Dizzy is a sideways belly
  flop; ko lies on his back with both boots up.

WARDROBE AND PROPS (locked — these appear in ALL frames, including the deaths):
  ALL 19 FRAMES: a one-piece hazmat suit in glossy golden yellow, crinkled all over with fine
  quilted creases and bright highlights, with a dark grey seam strip running down the front.
  The hood is part of the suit and holds a big, clear, curved visor window rimmed in grey
  that frames his whole face, with pale blue-white reflections on the glass. A charcoal-grey
  rubber respirator with metal collar fittings sits at the bottom edge of the visor over his
  chin, and a charcoal ribbed hose runs from it down across his chest and round to his back.
  On his back are silver-grey metal air tanks with dark bands (one shows from the front, two
  from the side), held by dark grey harness straps over the shoulders and round his middle;
  in the runs, dash-run and flee a second loose ribbed hose with a metal end trails out
  behind them. His gloves are thick dark grey rubber gauntlets, and his boots are dark grey
  glossy rubber with thick treaded soles. His own bushy ringed tail, tan and dark brown,
  sticks out of the back of the suit, low down, in every frame except shield, splash and ko.
  Per-frame props, and nothing else ever: a takeaway coffee cup (cream paper, kraft-brown
  sleeve, white lid) held up in both gloves in coffee, right where the respirator sits, so the
  mask and its hose are hidden behind it, with the visor fogged up grey inside, pink jitter
  squiggles around him and orange flames at his boots; a whirl of gold crimped-edge coins and
  golden fry sticks round him in magnet, with one coin stuck against the visor; a black
  umbrella with a crook handle held in his left glove in umbrella, dripping; a violet bubble
  with white-blue lightning veins in shield; a red fries carton full of golden fries in eat,
  with one fry pushed up against the respirator where his mouth would be. Effects only: small
  white jet spurts under his boots in leap (paint them blue-white, never magenta), blue-white
  splash under land, orange flame bursts with a blue flare at his boots plus pale streaks
  behind dash-run, orange-red streaks behind flee, pink and gold four-point sparkles in cheer,
  two yellow stars on an orbit line in dizzy, three yellow stars in ko, and a blue-white water
  crown in splash, where the suit streams wet and darkens to ochre. The small purple blot
  under the hose in dizzy and behind the tanks in ko is a background leak, not a prop: never
  paint it, and no magenta anywhere.

HOW THIS BODY WORKS:
  Underneath he is a short, stout raccoon. The suit makes him round and puffy, with thick
  limbs, a big hood and big boots, so he reads as a yellow barrel with a fishbowl face. The
  only raccoon on show is the face behind the visor and the tail at the back. The face is
  tawny brown: a dark brown bandit mask, cream brows and muzzle, a black nose, whiskers, and
  amber-brown eyes (sleepy and smug in idle, umbrella, sit and eat; a narrowed scowl in
  crouch; wide and round in leap, land, the runs, dash-run, flee, magnet, scared, cheer and
  splash; wide with reddish pupils in coffee; squeezed shut in shield; white spirals in dizzy;
  closed in ko). His pink tongue lolls out past the respirator in dizzy and ko. The visor
  always stays clear glass in front of his face: it fogs over completely only in coffee, a
  frosty rim of condensation gathers along the bottom of the glass in leap, scared, sit and
  cheer, and it streams with water only in splash. The hood never comes off, the respirator
  and its hose are attached in every frame where the coffee cup is not covering them, and the
  hose is always dark and ribbed, never smooth. The tail is the one soft thing on him, and in
  scared it puffs up to twice its size. He volunteered for the bin, and every frame should
  look like he still has questions about it.
corrections: Visor fog: a frosty rim of condensation also shows along the bottom of the glass in leap, scared, sit and cheer. 'Fogs only in coffee' was wrong; only the full fog-over is unique to coffee.
Coffee: the respirator and hose are not visible, because the cup is held where the mask sits. The block said the cup was held against the respirator and that the respirator is always attached.
Respirator: it is charcoal-grey rubber with metal collar fittings, not a black canister. The hose is charcoal.
Tail: it is not visible in shield, splash or ko. It is ringed tan and dark brown, not warm brown.
Flee streaks are orange-red only. The blue appears only as a flare at his boots in dash-run, which also has orange flame bursts.
Leap jet spurts: the reference has a pink-violet base. They are rewritten as white spurts to paint blue-white, never magenta.
Air tanks: one shows from the front and two from the side. This resolves the writer's note.
Stance: added magnet (arms up), umbrella (glove on belly), scared (gloves at the respirator), cheer (one knee kicked high) and splash (one boot kicked).
Eyes: added eat to the sleepy list, a crouch scowl, wide eyes in leap, land, the runs, magnet and cheer, reddish pupils in coffee, and the lolling tongue in dizzy and ko.
Splash: the soaked suit darkens to ochre.
Shield: the lightning veins are white-blue.
unsure: The respirator reads as attached at the lower rim of the visor, outside the glass; not confirmed whether it is meant to be inside or outside.
The purple blot in dizzy and ko looks like a background key leak, not a prop.
A faint pink-violet reflection on the visor edge in crouch, run-r and ko could be intended glare or a key leak.
The flying items in magnet read as gold coins plus golden fry sticks; some may be meant as gold bars.
In coffee the respirator and hose are completely absent; they may be hidden by the cup or simply missing from the art.
draftUnsure: The respirator reads as attached at the lower rim of the visor, outside the glass; I could not confirm whether it is meant to be inside or outside.
Only one air tank is visible from the front; two show clearly in the side views.
The purple blot in dizzy and ko looks like a background key leak, not a prop.
A faint pink-violet reflection sits on the right edge of the visor in some frames (run-r, ko); it could be intended glare or a key leak.
The flying items in magnet read as gold coins plus golden fry sticks; some may be meant as gold bars.

pirate.block:
Pirate Jimothy — one of the playable characters in Jimothy, a storybook hopper set on the
rainy streets of Seattle.

STANCE (locked — the same in every frame):
  Upright bipedal raccoon on two booted feet. He is never on all fours. Idle, coffee,
  magnet, umbrella and cheer stand square on both boots with the feet planted apart, and in
  idle one paw sits on his hip. Scared cringes with the knees drawn in and the head ducked
  to one side. Crouch is a low squat with one forepaw spread flat on the ground. Leap tucks
  both boots up under him in mid-air with one arm flung wide, and land is a wide knees-bent
  squat with both arms flung out. Run-l, run-r, dash-run and flee are a full two-legged
  sprint, torso tipped forward and coat tails flying back. Run-l and run-r are exact mirror
  images, dash-run faces right, and flee faces left with one paw clamping the hat down.
  Shield is a braced crouch with one open paw raised, sit and eat are flat on his rump with
  boots forward, dizzy is belly-down with one cheek on the ground, and ko is flat on his
  back with one boot kicked up.

WARDROBE AND PROPS (locked — these appear in ALL frames, including the deaths):
  ALL 19 FRAMES: a battered charcoal-black tricorn hat with rust-brown scuff marks and thin
  tarnished-gold piping along every edge (a small gold coin badge shows on its front in
  magnet and scared). Under it, a crimson bandana tied flat across the brow and knotted at
  the side, with two ragged torn-point tails that flutter. A single gold hoop earring with a
  small red bead hangs on the same side as the bandana knot, on the back side of his head
  away from where his snout points; the sheet tints the bead pinkish in a few frames, and it
  stays red. A black leather eye patch on a thin black strap covers his RIGHT eye (run-l,
  being a mirror, moves it to the left eye). A long deep-teal frock coat has a wide
  folded-back collar, wide turned-back cuffs, rows of small brass buttons down the fronts
  and cuffs, rust flecks, and a hem shredded into ragged strips. Under it: a cream linen
  shirt with a laced V neck (dark cord criss-crossed through eyelets), a wide crimson sash
  wound at the waist and knotted at his left hip with frayed ends hanging toward the knee,
  baggy dark-brown breeches, and tan-brown leather boots with folded-down cuffs and a brass
  buckle over the instep.
  THE SPYGLASS: a multi-draw brass telescope with a blue glass lens. It never leaves him and
  shows in 18 frames: raised beside his cheek with the lens pointing outward (idle); held
  out in one paw (crouch, land); raised high (leap, magnet, cheer) or at shoulder height
  (splash); clutched against his middle (run-l, run-r, dash-run, flee, shield); tucked at
  his hip below the sash (coffee) or through the sash (umbrella); pinned under his arm
  beside the fry carton (eat); held across his lap in both paws (sit); gripped in his paw on
  the ground (dizzy); lying across his chest (ko). In eat and ko the sheet paints its middle
  barrel red. Scared is the one frame where it cannot be seen: there both paws grip his
  coat. Leap shows one more short brass tube tucked upright in the sash, and land shows two.
  Per-frame props and effects, and nothing else ever: a takeaway cup with a brown sleeve and
  white lid, a curl of steam and small orange flames licking round his boots (coffee); gold
  coins and short gold bars flying in and sticking all over his coat and sash (magnet); a
  black umbrella beaded with rain on a thin brass shaft ending in a brass crook (umbrella);
  a violet crackling bubble around his crouch (shield); a plain red fry carton heaped with
  fries, with one fry held between his teeth (eat); white-gold four-point sparkles (cheer);
  three yellow stars circling on a thin orbit line (dizzy, ko); a pale blue water burst up
  to his waist with the hat dripping (splash); a white and pale blue splash at the boots
  (land); horizontal speed streaks with a white-gold flash at the boots (dash-run); orange
  flame streaks trailing off the coat hem and boots, with pale speed lines (flee). The sheet
  tints the dash-run streaks and the cheer sparkles hot pink and stains the base of the land
  splash violet; a repaint keeps them white, gold and pale blue. No magenta anywhere.

HOW THIS BODY WORKS:
  This is Jimothy's own raccoon under the costume: short, stocky and round-bellied with a
  big head. He has grey and cream fur, a full black mask, a cream muzzle, a black nose and
  long white whiskers. His one open eye is warm brown in the calm frames (idle, crouch,
  leap, umbrella, sit) and turns into a big white eye with a small black pupil when he is
  startled or whooping (land, magnet, cheer, dash-run, flee, coffee, scared, splash); in eat
  it is shut in contentment. His paws are dark charcoal with five fingers. The tail is BIG,
  not stubby: a full bushy cream-and-black ringed brush with four or five black bands. It
  pokes out from under the coat and sweeps behind him in most frames, but the sheet leaves
  it out of land, dash-run, flee, coffee and ko and shows only a scrap of fur behind his leg
  in splash.
  He reads at a glance as a triangle of three things: hat, eye patch and brass spyglass. The
  sheet breaks the patch in several frames. Coffee draws both eyes wide and bare, and
  dash-run draws its one visible eye bare with only the strap crossing his cheek; a repaint
  puts the patch back over the right eye in both. Flee shows a single bare eye with the patch
  out of view, dizzy puts a black-and-white spiral eye under the strap where the patch should
  sit, and in ko his eyes are shut and the patch cannot be told from the mask. His
  expression swings from a calm smile (idle) and a sly half-lidded smirk (crouch, umbrella,
  sit) to open-mouthed fanged whoops (leap, land, magnet, cheer), a toothy grin (run-l,
  run-r), gritted-teeth grimaces (shield, coffee, scared) and an open-mouthed yell
  (dash-run, flee, splash). His height, head size and coat length hold across all 19.
corrections: Idle: the spyglass is not at his eye. He holds it raised beside his cheek with the lens pointing outward, and he is not looking through it.

Stance: scared is not a bow-legged swagger. It is a cringe with the knees drawn in and the head ducked. The other standing frames stand square with the feet apart, so 'bow-legged' was dropped. Added the paw on the hip in idle, the raised open paw in shield and the flung arm in leap.
Dizzy is belly-down with one cheek on the ground and the face turned to the viewer, not face-down.
Tail: the claim that it shows in every upright frame is wrong. No tail is visible in land, dash-run, flee, coffee or ko, and splash shows only a scrap of fur behind the leg.

Eye colour: brown only in the calm frames (idle, crouch, leap, umbrella, sit). Land, magnet, cheer, dash-run, flee, coffee, scared and splash draw a big white eye with a black pupil, and eat has the eye shut.

Eye patch: 'both eyes wide open' was wrong for dash-run and flee, which show only one eye each. Dash-run shows a bare eye with the strap crossing the cheek. In flee (facing left) the patched side is simply out of view. Coffee is the only frame with two bare eyes. Also added dizzy's spiral eye sitting under the strap.
Expressions: coffee and scared are gritted-teeth grimaces, not yells. Shield is a grimace, run-l and run-r are toothy grins, and eat has the eyes shut. The idle smile is calm rather than half-lidded.
Coat collar is a wide folded-back lapel collar, not turned-up.

Spyglass: the 'never lets go' wording was changed, because it is tucked away in coffee, umbrella and eat. In coffee it sits at the hip below the sash, in eat it is pinned under his arm, and in splash it is raised to shoulder height. The running frames hold it against his middle, not his chest. 'Two-draw' and 'dark blue lens' became 'multi-draw' and 'blue glass lens'.
Added: the sheet paints the spyglass's middle barrel red in eat and ko.
Added: leap shows one extra short brass tube tucked upright in the sash, and land shows two.
Magnet: the gold bars also stick to the sash, and there is a clustered bunch at his middle.
Eat: the carton is plain red and heaped with fries.

Effects colours: the dash-run streaks and cheer sparkles are painted hot pink, the land splash has a violet base, and the earring bead reads pinkish in some frames. The block now keeps them white, gold, pale blue and red.
Flee: the flames trail off both the coat hem and the boots, with pale speed lines behind.
unsure: Dizzy draws a black-and-white spiral eye under the patch strap. It is unclear whether that gag is allowed or whether a repaint should keep the patch, so the block does not order a fix.
In ko his eyes are shut, and I cannot tell the patch from the black mask.
The extra brass tubes in the sash in leap (one) and land (two) could be a second spyglass, a pistol grip or drift.
The magnet gold sticks read as bars, but the bunched cluster at his sash looks like fries.
The red middle barrel on the spyglass in eat and ko may be intended or may be drift.
The grey scrap behind his leg in splash may be the tail tip.
The earring and bandana knot swap ears with facing (his right ear in idle and scared, his left in crouch, umbrella, sit and eat), so no fixed ear is locked.
draftUnsure: Eye patch in dizzy and ko: in dizzy a black-and-white spiral eye sits where the patched eye should be, and in ko the eyes are shut and I cannot tell whether the dark patch over one eye is the patch or just his mask.

The eye patch is missing in dash-run, flee and coffee (both eyes drawn wide and bare). I wrote this up as a break from the model, but that is an assumption; the Director may have allowed it on purpose.
I could not find the spyglass in scared. It may be hidden behind the coat or tail.
The flying gold sticks in magnet could be gold bars or fries; I described them only as 'short gold sticks'.
In ko the spyglass barrel reads red. That may be the sash showing under a brass tube, or a red leather barrel.
The gold coin badge on the hat front shows only in magnet and scared; elsewhere the angle may simply hide it.

Which ear carries the earring and bandana knot changes with facing (idle and scared show it on his right ear, crouch and umbrella on his left). I described it as 'the back side of his head' rather than naming a fixed ear.

astronaut.block:
Astronaut Jimothy — one of the playable characters in Jimothy, a storybook hopper set on the
rainy streets of Seattle.

STANCE (locked — the same in every frame):
  Upright bipedal on two big boots, heavy and waddling, like a toddler in a snowsuit. He is
  never on all fours. In idle one glove rests on his hip while the other taps the side of
  the helmet. Crouch is a deep forward hunch with one glove flat on the ground. Leap has
  knees tucked with the boot soles showing, one fist punched up and the other arm out. Land
  is a wide squat with both arms flung out. Run-l and run-r are exact mirror images: a
  two-legged stride with fists pumping. Dash-run and flee BOTH face right, and in flee one
  open glove reaches forward. Coffee and cheer stand square on both boots, magnet throws both
  open gloves up, and scared is a wide-legged cringe with both gloves clutched at his chest.
  Shield is down on one knee with one glove raised. Sit and eat are on his rump with boot
  soles to the viewer. Dizzy is belly-down, and ko is on his back with both boots up and one
  kicked high.

WARDROBE AND PROPS (locked — these appear in ALL frames, including the deaths):
  ALL 19 FRAMES: a round, clear fishbowl helmet enclosing his whole head, with a soft white
  highlight near the top. The helmet sits in a metal neck ring striped with a thin rust-red
  band. The sheet paints the glass rim a hot pink-violet glow in most frames and lilac in
  umbrella and splash, and fills the whole bubble with pink haze in coffee. A repaint keeps
  the glass clear with a pale rim, and the rim is never magenta. The suit is a puffy,
  quilted, cream spacesuit with a soft crinkled texture and rust-red piping at the cuffs and
  boot tops. It carries two round navy patches with orange rims: an orange ringed planet on
  his right shoulder (the viewer's left) and a white rocket with an orange flame on his left
  chest (the viewer's right). Umbrella draws the whole figure flipped, with the pack on the
  viewer's right and the planet on the viewer's-right shoulder. Mid-chest is a small square
  cream control box with corner bolts and one round blue button; sit shrinks it to a small
  grey tag, and the fry carton hides it in eat. On his back is a boxy cream life-support
  pack with small rust-red square lights and a thin antenna ending in a little metal ball. A
  ribbed navy hose loops from the pack round to the front of the suit. He wears dark grey
  five-fingered gloves and chunky dark-grey moon boots with thick treaded soles.
  Per-frame props and effects, and nothing else ever: small white four-point sparkles below
  him (leap); pale blue-white impact spikes at the boots (land); blue-white jet flames from
  the boot soles plus speed lines (dash-run, where both boots fire, and flee, where only the
  back boot fires); red alarm tick marks over the helmet (flee); a takeaway cup with a brown
  sleeve and white lid held in both gloves, jitter squiggles, orange flames round the boots
  and the glass fogged so his fur reads paler (coffee); crimped gold bottle caps with a navy
  centre and a red star, and short orange fry sticks, swirling round him on curved trails
  (magnet); a black umbrella dripping rain, on a thin dark shaft with a crook handle
  (umbrella); a violet honeycomb bubble (shield); a red fry carton with one fry in his teeth
  (eat), where the sheet shows a small yellow arch mark on the carton that stays a blank
  smudge and never becomes a letter or brand mark; gold and pale lilac-white four-point
  sparkles (cheer); spiral eyes, tongue out and yellow orbiting stars (dizzy); a pale blue
  water burst that sprays up past the helmet, with water streaming down the suit and glass
  (splash); rolled-back eyes, tongue out and three yellow stars (ko). No magenta anywhere.

HOW THIS BODY WORKS:
  He is a round, heavy little raccoon who is almost all suit. The suit gives him a barrel
  body, stubby quilted limbs and big boots, and only his head shows, inside the glass. His
  face has dark brown-grey fur, a cream stripe above a black mask band, cream cheeks and
  muzzle, a black nose and whiskers. His eyes are small, dark and half-lidded when he is smug
  (idle, crouch, umbrella, sit, shield), huge and white with black pupils when he is startled
  or thrilled (leap, land, run-l, run-r, dash-run, flee, coffee, magnet, scared, splash), and
  squeezed shut in a grin in eat and cheer. NO TAIL is visible in any of the 19 frames; it
  is sealed inside the suit, and no repaint may add one.
  The glass is always a full sphere seated on the neck ring, with the head always inside it
  and never poking through. The blue hose shows in every frame. The pack antenna shows in 14
  frames; the sheet leaves it out of coffee, magnet, cheer, dizzy and splash. At a glance he
  is a cream marshmallow with a bubble on top and a blue hose looped around him. Every move
  plays a little slow and puffy, so even the leap is a hop in a snowsuit. Head-to-suit
  proportion is identical everywhere except crouch, where the sheet draws the helmet and
  head noticeably larger; repaints keep crouch at the idle proportion.
corrections: Patches: the planet sits on his right shoulder, not the chest. The rocket is on his left chest and has an orange flame. Both patches have orange rims. Umbrella draws the whole figure flipped (pack and planet on the viewer's right).
The antenna is not always there. It is missing in coffee, magnet, cheer, dizzy and splash, so it shows in 14 frames.
Control box: sit shows only a small grey tag in its place, and the fry carton hides it in eat.
Gloves are dark grey rather than dark charcoal.
Magnet: the caps are crimped gold bottle caps with a navy centre and a red star.
Jet flames: both boots fire in dash-run, but only the back boot fires in flee.
Splash: the burst sprays up behind him past the helmet, and water streams down the suit and glass. It does not stop at his chest.
Eyes: added leap, run-l, run-r, dash-run, flee and magnet to the big white-eye list and shield to the smug list. Eat and cheer have the eyes squeezed shut.
Face: added the cream stripe above the mask and the cream muzzle.
Coffee: the whole bubble is filled with pink haze, not only the rim.
Stance: added coffee and cheer standing square, magnet with both gloves up, scared as a wide-legged cringe, the raised glove in shield, the boot soles showing in leap, and both boots up in ko.
Eat line: replaced the em dash with a clause, and described the carton mark as a yellow arch shape.
Cheer sparkles are gold and pale lilac-white.
unsure: The hot pink-violet helmet rim could be the intended glass tint or spill from the magenta key colour. The block forbids magenta and asks for a pale rim, which needs a Director call.
The antenna is missing in five frames. It may be hidden by the angle or the art may have drifted.
The yellow arch mark on the eat carton resembles a real fast-food logo, and the block keeps it a blank smudge.
In crouch the head and helmet are drawn larger, which I treated as drift.
No tail is visible anywhere. I assumed it is sealed inside the suit, as the writer did.
Umbrella flips the figure, so whether a repaint should un-flip it (planet back on the viewer's left) is a Director call.
draftUnsure: The hot pink-violet glow on the helmet rim, visible in most frames, could be the intended glass tint or spill from the magenta key colour. I cannot tell which from the sheet, so the block forbids magenta and asks for a pale rim. This needs a Director call.
No tail is visible in any frame. I assumed it is meant to be sealed inside the suit, not accidentally left out.
The magnet discs look like crimped gold bottle caps with a star centre, and the orange sticks look like fries. At that size I could not confirm either.
The fry carton in eat has a small yellow mark that resembles a real fast-food logo. The block says to keep it a blank smudge.
In coffee the helmet looks fogged and his fur reads paler. That may be deliberate steam, or drift.
In crouch the head and helmet are drawn noticeably larger. I treated that as drift.

alien.block:
Little Green Jimothy — one of the playable characters in Jimothy, a storybook hopper set on
the rainy streets of Seattle.

STANCE (locked — the same in every frame):
  Upright bipedal on two silver boots, and never on all fours. In idle one glove is planted
  on his hip and his weight sits on one leg. Crouch is a forward hunch with one glove
  splayed on the ground. In leap one arm waves up, the other reaches out and one knee comes
  high. Land is a squat with both arms out. Run-l and run-r are exact mirror images: a
  two-legged stride with fists pumping. Dash-run faces right, and flee faces left with one
  glove clamped to the top of the hood. Magnet and cheer fling both arms up, and cheer kicks
  one knee high. Scared leans back on bent knees with both gloves clutched at his chest.
  Shield is down on one knee with both gloves up. Sit has him on his rump with his arms
  folded, and eat is also on his rump. Dizzy is belly-down, and ko is on his back with both
  feet kicked up.

WARDROBE AND PROPS (locked — these appear in ALL frames, including the deaths):
  ALL 19 FRAMES: a one-piece chrome-silver alien onesie, glossy with bright reflections and
  soft padded seams. The "green" in his name is the belly panel and the glow; the suit
  itself is silver. The hood frames his face in a round opening. It carries two huge glossy
  black bulging eyes set on top like a frog's, with teal glints, plus a scatter of small
  punched dots. Two long antennae of dark beaded chain rise from it, each ending in a
  glowing mint-cyan orb; ko is the one frame where the sheet leaves them off. A row of small
  silver spikes runs down the back of the hood and along the spine, seen whenever his back
  or side is turned. At the neck sits a wide riveted pewter collar set with small teal studs.
  On the front is a pale mint-green belly panel, topped by a round glowing cyan gem in a
  silver bezel. He wears silver five-fingered gloves and silver boots with rounded toe
  bumps; the soles show padded toes in leap, run-l, run-r, flee, sit, eat, cheer and ko.
  Per-frame props and effects, and nothing else ever: cyan four-point sparkles (leap); a
  white splash with a lilac tint at the boots (land); blue-white speed streaks and a small
  splash off the back heel (dash-run); red and blue speed streaks (flee); a takeaway cup
  with a brown sleeve and white lid, a curl of steam, jitter squiggles and orange flames at
  the boots (coffee); gold bottle caps and short golden fry sticks flying round him, with
  one cap stuck to his collar (magnet); a translucent lilac umbrella beaded with rain, on a
  thin black shaft with a black crook handle (umbrella); a violet honeycomb bubble (shield);
  a plain white paper fry carton, with one fry in his teeth and one stuck to his belly (eat);
  red, gold and blue four-point sparkles (cheer); spiral eyes, tongue out, drooping antennae
  and yellow stars (dizzy); a pale blue water burst with the whole suit streaming wet
  (splash); white cross eyes, tongue out and three yellow stars (ko). No magenta anywhere.

HOW THIS BODY WORKS:
  He is a chunky, round-bellied raccoon in a costume, not an actual alien. The only animal
  showing is his face and his tail. His face has warm brown fur, tan cheeks and muzzle, a
  dark-brown mask, a black nose, whiskers and big pale yellow-cream eyes with dark pupils.
  The tail is a full bushy ring-tail in tan and dark-brown bands, coming out the back of the
  onesie and visible in every frame except land.
  The two black hood eyes are costume, and they never blink, never move and never become his
  real eyes. His own eyes always stay in the face opening. Wherever the antennae show there
  are exactly two, always beaded and always tipped with glowing orbs, and they bob and trail
  with motion. At a glance he is a shiny silver bean with frog eyes on top, a mint belly and
  two glowing bobbles. The sheet drifts in two places. In coffee the suit turns glassy teal
  and one boot goes brass-tan, and in eat the sleeve of the fry hand goes gold. Both stay
  chrome silver in any repaint.
corrections: Antennae are not always present. Ko shows no antennae at all, so 'there are always exactly two' was reworded.
The tail is not visible in land, so 'visible in every frame' was wrong.
Padded toe soles show in leap, run-l, run-r, flee, sit, eat, cheer and ko, not only in sit and ko.
Ko eyes are white cross marks.
Cheer sparkles are red, gold and blue, not only red and blue.
Coffee cup: added the white lid.
The dash-run splash comes off the back heel.
Stance: added magnet and cheer with arms flung up, the high knee in cheer, and scared leaning back with both gloves at his chest.
Dizzy: added the drooping antennae. Face: the tan colour covers the muzzle as well as the cheeks.
Land splash is white with a lilac tint.
unsure: The finger count on the silver gloves looks like five, but the art is small.
The umbrella is translucent lilac, unlike the black umbrellas on other skins. Whether that is intended is unconfirmed.
The glassy teal suit and brass-tan boot in coffee and the gold sleeve in eat are treated as drift. That is not confirmed.
The small punched dots on the hood could be rivets, vents or plain texture.
The tail is painted as real fur in every frame. Whether it comes through a hole in the suit or is part of the costume is unclear.
The missing antennae in ko could be drift or could be hidden by the angle.
The magnet sticks read as fries but could be gold bars.
draftUnsure: The exact finger count on the silver gloves. They read as five-fingered in idle, magnet and ko, but the art is small.
The umbrella is translucent lilac, unlike the black umbrellas on other skins. I could not tell whether that colour is intended.
In coffee one boot reads brass-tan and the suit turns glassy teal, and in eat the fry-hand sleeve reads gold. I called all three drift, but I cannot confirm that.
Whether the small punched dots on the hood are meant as rivets, vents or plain texture.
Whether the tail is meant to be a real fur tail through a hole in the suit or part of the costume. It is painted as fur in every frame.

disco.block:
Disco Jimothy — one of the playable characters in Jimothy, a storybook hopper set on the
rainy streets of Seattle.

STANCE (locked — the same in every frame):
  Upright bipedal showman who is never on all fours: weight on one bent leg, hip cocked, and
  an index finger doing the pointing. He points up in idle, leap, magnet and cheer (cheer's
  other hand points out sideways), and straight out sideways in run-l and run-r. In idle one
  hand is on his hip and the other points up and out. Crouch is a deep lunge with one hand
  flat on the ground and the other arm flung up. Leap points skyward with one knee high.
  Land is a wide squat with one hand touching down and the other flung out. Run-l and run-r
  are exact mirror images: a strutting sideways stride with one arm pointing ahead and the
  other fist at the belt. Dash-run and flee both face right, and in flee one hand is up at
  his sunglasses. Coffee stands square with the cup in both hands. Shield is a low lunge
  with one hand at the glasses. Scared is knock-kneed with both hands up at his chin. Sit is
  on his rump with one elbow propped on a raised knee. Eat is on his rump with his knees up.
  Dizzy lies on his side, and ko is flat on his back with both platforms in the air.

WARDROBE AND PROPS (locked — these appear in ALL frames, including the deaths):
  ALL 19 FRAMES: a glossy cream-champagne satin jumpsuit with stitched panel seams. It has
  an enormous upturned, pointed collar of turquoise sequins, edged in gold and flecked with
  gold glitter, opening into a deep V. Wide turquoise sequin cuffs dotted with small gold
  stars circle both wrists. The bell-bottom flares have tall pointed turquoise sequin flame
  inserts outlined in gold and dotted with gold stars, rising from a turquoise sequin band at
  the hem. He wears a gold studded belt with a round, mirror-faceted disco-ball buckle and a
  heavy gold chain carrying a big round gold medallion engraved with a disco-ball grid. On
  his face are gold aviator sunglasses with amber lenses, and on his feet are glossy gold
  platform shoes with thick stacked soles.
  Per-frame props and effects, and nothing else ever: a burst of pale sparks at the shoes
  (land); rainbow-edged speed streaks and star sparks (dash-run); red and orange-gold speed
  streaks (flee); a takeaway cup with a brown sleeve and white lid, a puff of steam over his
  head, jitter squiggles and flames round the shoes (coffee); flat gold coins and short
  golden bars spinning round him (magnet); a teal-and-gold panelled umbrella dripping rain,
  on a gold shaft with a gold crook handle (umbrella); a violet crackling bubble (shield); a
  red fry carton, with one fry held in his mouth like a toothpick and another pinched in his
  fingers (eat); four-point sparkles and a few gold coins (cheer); spiral eyes, tongue out,
  the sunglasses knocked askew with one reddish lens dangling, and yellow stars on an orbit
  line (dizzy); a pale blue water burst with the jumpsuit streaming wet (splash); tongue
  out, eyes shut behind crooked sunglasses and three yellow stars (ko). The sheet tints the
  land sparks, the dash-run streaks, the coffee steam and the cheer sparkles hot pink; a
  repaint keeps them white and gold. No magenta anywhere.
  Drift the sheet shows: in leap, run-l, run-r and dash-run the medallion swings low and
  reads as a plain gold disc with a cross, and in run-l, run-r and dash-run it hides the
  mirror buckle. Land swaps the mirror buckle for a plain rectangular gold one. Flee swings a
  second gold disc out on the chain beside the grid medallion. A small dark-red cloth or
  pouch peeks from behind him in leap, land, dash-run, coffee, sit and ko, with a sliver of
  red behind the shoulder in run-l and run-r. It is absent from idle, so it is not part of
  the costume.

HOW THIS BODY WORKS:
  He is lean and long-legged, with a narrow waist and limbs made even longer by the flares.
  His fur is brownish grey and a little tufty on the crown and cheeks, with a cream stripe
  above the black mask, a cream muzzle, the mask showing around and behind the lenses, and a
  black nose. His hands are dark charcoal with five fingers, and the pointing index finger is
  his signature. The tail is a full, bushy, grey-brown ring-tail with dark bands, poking out
  behind the jumpsuit in most frames; the sheet hides it in leap, land, dash-run, coffee and
  dizzy.
  At a glance he is gold glasses, turquoise collar points, gold platforms and a pointing
  finger. The glasses sit square on his face in most frames. In land and scared they slide
  down his nose and his round eyes peer over the top, in ko they sit crooked, and in dizzy
  they are knocked half off. Elsewhere his eyes are drawn through the amber lenses:
  half-lidded cool in idle, crouch, leap, run-l, run-r, magnet, umbrella, shield, sit, eat
  and cheer, and perfectly round and bug-eyed in dash-run, flee, coffee and splash. The satin
  always shines, and the sequins always glitter even in the rain.
corrections: Glasses: they do not sit on his face in 17 frames. In land and scared they slide down his nose and his round eyes peer over the top. In ko they are crooked on his face, and in dizzy they are knocked half off with a reddish lens dangling.
Eyes: scared moved out of the 'through the lenses' list. Leap, magnet, shield and cheer were added to the half-lidded list.
Collar: it is flecked with gold glitter rather than clearly studded with stars. The small gold stars are on the cuffs and flares.
Land: the belt shows a plain rectangular gold buckle, not the mirror ball.
The medallion also reads as a plain gold disc with a cross in leap. Flee swings a second gold disc out on the chain beside the grid medallion.
Red pouch: a sliver of red also shows behind the shoulder in run-l and run-r.
Tail: it is hidden in leap, land, dash-run, coffee and dizzy.
