Removed 'leaner and longer-legged than most of the cast', a comparison this sheet cannot support.
Eat: a second fry is pinched in his fingers besides the one in his mouth.
Flee streaks are red and orange-gold.
Effects colours: the hot pink tint on the land sparks, dash-run streaks, coffee steam and cheer sparkles is now named and kept white and gold.
Stance: added coffee standing square and scared knock-kneed with his hands at his chin.
Magnet sticks described as short golden bars. Face: added the cream stripe above the mask. Ko: his eyes are shut behind the crooked glasses.
unsure: Whether the dark-red cloth or pouch behind him is part of the costume needs a Director call. It reads as a bag in land and dash-run and as a cape flap in coffee and ko.
The medallion shows a cross in leap, run-l, run-r and dash-run and a grid elsewhere. It could be the medallion's other face or drift.
The magnet sticks could be fries or gold bars.
In dizzy the dangling lens reads reddish, not amber.
In ko there is a small brown tuft near his hip that might be the tail.
The second gold disc swinging in flee may be drift or a second pendant.
draftUnsure: The dark-red cloth or pouch behind him in leap, land, dash-run, coffee, sit and ko. It reads as a small pouch in land and dash-run and as a cape flap in coffee and ko. It is absent from idle, so I treated it as not part of the costume; that needs a Director call.

In run-l, run-r and dash-run the medallion reads as a gold disc with a cross rather than the disco-ball grid seen in idle. I cannot tell whether that is the medallion or the belt buckle seen from the side.
The golden sticks in magnet could be fries or gold bars.
In dizzy the lenses of the knocked-off sunglasses look reddish, not amber.
The steam puff over his head in coffee has a pink tint. I described it only as steam.

robot.block:
Robot Jimothy — one of the playable characters in Jimothy, a storybook hopper set on the
rainy streets of Seattle.

STANCE (locked — the same in every frame):
  Upright bipedal machine, stiff and jointed, and never on all fours. In idle one hand is on
  his hip and the other fist is raised at shoulder height. Crouch is a deep forward crouch
  with one hand flat on the ground and the other arm cocked back. Leap has both fists up and
  knees tucked. Land is a low squat with one hand down and the other arm out. Run-l and
  run-r are exact mirror images: an upright sprint with fists pumping. Dash-run faces right.
  Flee faces left, one arm thrown forward and the other flung back, with the tail streaming
  behind. Coffee stands square with the cup in both hands, magnet throws both open hands up,
  scared clutches his chest with both hands, and cheer punches one fist up. Shield is a
  crouch with one hand over his face. Sit and eat are upright on his rump with his knees up.
  Dizzy is curled on his side, and ko is on his back with his feet up.

WARDROBE AND PROPS (locked — these appear in ALL frames, including the deaths):
  No clothing; he IS the machine. ALL 19 FRAMES: his head is made of riveted, brushed-steel
  plates sculpted into a raccoon face, with pointed ears, a painted dark mask band, a pale
  muzzle and a black nose. There is a short cylindrical bolt knob on each side of the head.
  A stubby post on the crown carries a thin curved wire antenna with a red ball on the end.
  He has round glowing yellow eyes with black pupils. His chest is a boxy riveted steel
  plate with a row of three round indicator lights: green, yellow, red, reading left to
  right in front views (the mirror flips the order in run-l, and it runs vertically in
  dizzy). On his back is a boxy riveted steel pack. His hands have jointed steel fingers,
  and his feet are steel paws with toes.
  Per-frame props and effects, and nothing else ever: blue-white electric sparks crackling
  at the feet (leap, dash-run); blue-white splash spikes at the feet (land); red and blue
  speed streaks with a red flare shooting back from behind his pack (flee); a takeaway cup
  with a brown sleeve and white lid, a curl of steam, jitter squiggles, a red starburst spark
  in place of the antenna ball and orange flames round the feet (coffee); crimped gold
  bottle caps and short knobbed gold sticks swirling on curved red trails, with caps stuck
  to his head, cheek and chest and a blue spark over the antenna (magnet); a black umbrella
  dripping rain, on a thin grey shaft with a brown wooden crook handle (umbrella); a violet
  crackled bubble, with a small gold glint in the hand at his chest (shield); blue alarm
  tick marks round his head (scared); a red fry carton with one fry in his mouth (eat); gold
  and blue four-point sparkles (cheer); yellow concentric-ring eyes, tongue out, a second
  red ball bouncing loose beside his head, and three yellow stars on a thin orbit line
  (dizzy); a pale blue water burst with blue sparks shorting across his chest (splash); the
  antenna bent flat sideways with its ball still on, tongue out, a blue spark at his hip and
  three yellow stars (ko). No magenta anywhere.

HOW THIS BODY WORKS:
  THE MODEL IS THE IDLE BUILD: a stocky tin raccoon with a squarish chest box, thick plated
  cylinder arms and legs, round knee caps and dark ribbed bellows at the shoulders, elbows,
  waist and knees. His head cheeks are painted with warm grey-brown fur strokes around a
  cream muzzle, and his tail is a soft ring-tail in grey and black bands. That build holds in
  idle, crouch, leap, land, run-l, run-r, dash-run, coffee, sit and eat.
  The sheet swaps in a SECOND, thinner build in flee, magnet, umbrella, shield, scared,
  cheer, dizzy, splash and ko. That build has an all-grey cartoon face with much bigger
  yellow eyes ringed in black, a rounder barrel torso, mostly spindly black ribbed rod arms
  and legs, and a chrome segmented tail, which even tapers into a drill cone in flee and
  shield. The two builds must never mix inside one frame, and a repaint goes back to the idle
  build. At a glance he is three traffic-light buttons, a red-ball antenna and yellow
  headlamp eyes on a raccoon face. The joke is that everything about him clanks except his
  smug expression.
corrections: Ko: the antenna ball is not knocked off. The antenna is bent flat sideways and the red ball is still on its tip.
Dizzy: the antenna keeps its own ball, and a second red ball bounces loose beside his head. Dizzy also shows three stars.
Flee: one arm is thrown forward and the other is flung back. Both arms are not forward.
The drill-cone tail also appears in shield, not only in flee.
The thin build's limbs are mostly black rods, but shield keeps plated arms, hence 'mostly'.
The bellows line moved out of the ALL 19 FRAMES list into the idle-build description, because the thin build has rod limbs instead of bellows joints.
Magnet: the discs are crimped gold bottle caps and the sticks are short and knobbed. Caps stick to his head, cheek and chest.
Umbrella: added the thin grey shaft.
Shield: added a small gold glint in the hand held at his chest.
Coffee cup: added the white lid. Land: the spikes are at the feet.
Stance: added coffee standing square, magnet with both hands open, scared clutching his chest and cheer punching one fist up.
Flee: the red flare shoots back from behind the pack.
unsure: Which build is canonical is a Director call. The chunky idle build appears in 10 frames and the thin rod-limbed build in 9. The block keeps the writer's choice of the idle build.
The finger count on the steel hands could not be confirmed.
The fan-shaped gold object at the upper left in magnet may be a bunch of fries, so it was left out.
The idle-build tail is painted with fur strokes, so it may be fur or painted metal.
The light order is partly hidden in shield and splash.
In dizzy, the loose red ball by his head could be read as the antenna ball popping off, but the antenna tip appears to keep its own ball.
draftUnsure: WHICH BUILD IS CANONICAL: the sheet is split almost evenly, with the chunky idle build in 10 frames and a thinner rod-limbed build in 9 (flee, magnet, umbrella, shield, scared, cheer, dizzy, splash, ko). I named the idle build as the model because it is frame 1 and the majority. That is my call, not something the sheet settles, and it needs Director confirmation before any repaint.
The finger count on the steel hands. The joints are visible, but I could not count fingers reliably.
Magnet has a small fan-shaped gold object at the upper left, possibly a bunch of fries. I left it out of the prop list.
Whether the idle-build tail is meant to be fur or painted metal. It is painted with fur strokes, while the thin build's tail is plainly chrome segments.
The eye-light order in shield and splash: partly hidden.

wizard.block:
Wizothy — one of the playable characters in Jimothy, a storybook hopper set on the rainy
streets of Seattle.

STANCE (locked — the same in every frame):
  Upright bipedal on bare, flat hind paws that show under the robe hem, and never on all
  fours. In idle one paw rests on his hip while the other raises the wand. Crouch is a
  forward hunch with one forepaw flat on the ground and the wand thrust back. Leap thrusts
  the wand up with knees tucked and the robe flaring. Land is a wide squat with the wand
  raised in one paw and the other arm out. Run-l and run-r are exact mirror images: a
  bounding two-legged stride with the cowl streaming and the wand held level at the waist.
  Dash-run and flee both face right, and in flee one paw clamps the hat down while the other
  points the wand ahead. Magnet and cheer hold the wand high, magnet with the other paw
  flung out and cheer with it at his chest. Shield is a crouch with the wand across his
  chest. Scared recoils onto one leg with one paw at his mouth. Sit and eat are on his rump
  with the robe pooled around him. Dizzy is belly-down, and ko is on his back with both hind
  soles up.

WARDROBE AND PROPS (locked — these appear in ALL frames, including the deaths):
  ALL 19 FRAMES: a floppy royal-navy wizard hat with a wide droopy brim. Its tall crown
  bends over at the tip and flops back, away from the way he faces, and it is printed with
  scattered gold five-point stars and one gold crescent moon. His ears poke out under the
  brim. He wears a long navy robe in the same cloth, sprinkled with gold stars and gold
  crescent moons. It has a draped cowl lying over the shoulders, wide bell sleeves, a frayed
  ankle-length hem and a gold crescent-moon clasp at the throat. A braided tan-gold rope
  belt is tied at the waist, with two tasselled ends hanging down the front.
  THE WAND: a thin brown wooden stick topped with a glowing pale-gold five-point star. He
  holds it raised (idle, leap, land, magnet, scared, cheer, splash), pointed out or back
  (crouch, flee), level at the waist (run-l, run-r, dash-run), across his chest (shield) or
  across his lap (sit). In umbrella it is carried low in one paw while the other holds the
  umbrella. In coffee it is tucked at the rope belt with only the star showing, and in eat
  it lies under the fry carton with the star hidden. It sits on the ground under his paw in
  dizzy and is clutched across his chest in ko, where the sheet loses the star and draws a
  plain knobbed stick. Leap also shows a short knobbed stick tucked through the rope belt
  while the wand is overhead.
  Per-frame props and effects, and nothing else ever: a sparkle trail off the star (leap,
  magnet, cheer); a white and pale blue splash at the paws (land); blue speed streaks, gold
  sparkles and a splash at the back paw (dash-run); orange zigzag lightning at the heels
  plus speed lines (flee); a takeaway cup with a brown sleeve and white lid, a curl of steam
  and orange flames round the paws (coffee); gold coins, some with rose-pink centres, and
  short golden fry sticks swirling round him, with a small dark-red splat at his side
  (magnet); a black umbrella dripping rain, on a thin black shaft with a brown crook handle
  (umbrella); a violet crackling bubble (shield); a red fry carton, with one fry in his
  mouth and one dropped on the robe (eat), where the sheet paints a yellow arch mark on the
  carton that stays a blank smudge and never becomes a letter or brand mark; blue, red and
  warm-orange four-point sparkles (cheer); spiral eyes, tongue out and two yellow stars on
  an orbit line (dizzy); a pale blue water burst with the robe soaked and streaming
  (splash); one X eye with the other squeezed shut, tongue out and three yellow stars (ko).
  No magenta anywhere.

HOW THIS BODY WORKS:
  This is Jimothy's own raccoon: small, round and short-legged, with grey-tan fur, a full
  black mask, cream brows and muzzle, a black nose, long whiskers, and dark eyes with white
  highlights (these go wide and white in leap, dash-run, flee, coffee, magnet, scared and
  splash). His forepaws are dark brown with five fingers, and his bare hind paws are dark
  brown and flat-footed. The tail is full and bushy, grey-tan with black rings, and sticks
  out from under the robe in every frame except splash and ko.
  The robe hides his body shape, so read motion off the flapping hem, the streaming cowl and
  the flopping hat tip, never off his body. The hat always sits low on his brow and stands
  about as tall as his whole head, and it never shrinks. At a glance he is navy cloth with
  gold stars, a star-tipped wand and a ringed tail. His face stays a smug half-lidded grin in
  idle, umbrella and sit, narrows to a sly smirk in crouch and land, and squints one eye
  shut in shield, which is the face of someone who has just made a bin lid slightly better.
corrections: Umbrella: the crook handle is brown, not black. The shaft is black.
Land: the wand is raised in one paw, not pointed out.
Tail: it is not visible in splash or ko, so 'in every frame' was wrong.
Leap: a second short knobbed stick is tucked through the rope belt while the wand is overhead.
Expression: shield is a one-eye squint, not half-lidded. Crouch and land are narrow-eyed smirks.
Wide white eyes also appear in leap and magnet.
Ko: one eye is an X and the other is squeezed shut.
Dizzy shows two stars on its orbit line.
Dash-run: added the gold sparkles and the splash at the back paw.
Cheer sparkles include red as well as blue and warm orange.
Flee: the other paw points the wand ahead.
Stance: added magnet and cheer, and the paw at his mouth in scared. The idle paw rests on his hip. In umbrella the wand is carried low.
Eat line: replaced the em dash with a clause, and described the carton mark as a yellow arch.
Land splash: described as white and pale blue.
unsure: In ko the wand is a plain knobbed stick with no star. The star may be lost or hidden.
The extra knobbed stick at the belt in leap could be a second wand or drift.
The yellow arch mark on the eat carton resembles a real fast-food logo, and the block keeps it a blank smudge.
In magnet, the dark-red splat and the rose-pink coin centres could be ketchup, an effect or stray marks.
The land splash has a violet stain at its base, and the wand star in splash has a pink tint. Both were left out of the block.
Which ear shows under the brim changes with facing, so no side is locked.
draftUnsure: In ko the wand is drawn as a plain knobbed stick with no star. I cannot tell whether the star is lost or just hidden under his paw.
In eat the wand lies under the carton and the star is not visible.
The fry carton in eat carries a yellow arch mark that looks like a real fast-food logo. The block says to keep it a blank smudge.
In magnet some of the gold coins have rose-pink centres, and there is a small dark-red splat by the robe. I cannot say whether the splat is ketchup, an effect, or a stray mark.
The land splash has a faint violet glint at the paws. I left that colour out of the block.
Which ear shows under the brim changes with facing. I did not lock a side.

barnacle.block:
The Barnacle — one of the playable characters in Jimothy, a storybook hopper set on the
rainy streets of Seattle.

STANCE (locked — the same in every frame):
  Upright biped on short, slightly bowed legs, flat-footed in his dress shoes at rest (idle,
  coffee, magnet, umbrella, scared, cheer); in idle one hand is up at his glasses and the
  other sits on his hip. He runs upright on two legs in run-l, run-r, dash-run and flee,
  belly first, fists pumping, jacket flying (in flee one hand is up at his glasses instead).
  A hand only touches the ground when he gets low: crouch and land are wide forward squats
  with one flat palm planted on the pavement and the other arm reaching out. Leap is
  airborne with one hand flung high, one knee up and the other arm reaching down. Shield is
  a squat with one palm raised and the other hand at his tie; cheer has one hand thrown high
  and the other on his chest. Sit and eat are on his rump with both shoes out front (hands
  on his knees in sit); dizzy is a belly-down sprawl with his face turned to us and both
  arms splayed; ko is flat on his back with both shoes kicked up in the air, soles showing.
  He is never four-square and never on his knuckles.

WARDROBE AND PROPS (locked — these appear in ALL frames, including the deaths):
  ALL 19 FRAMES: a black single-breasted suit jacket (notch lapels, buttoned cuffs with the
  white shirt cuff showing; its hem flares out behind him in leap, run-l, run-r, dash-run
  and flee), a cream-white dress shirt with a chest pocket, stretched tight over the belly
  with the collar open, a thin gold chain necklace at the open collar, black trousers on a
  black belt with a small dull brass buckle, glossy black leather dress shoes, and round
  thin gold wire glasses with amber-orange tinted lenses and dark tortoiseshell arms. The
  glasses never leave his face: knocked crooked in scared, spiral eyes behind them in dizzy,
  dripping in splash, eyes squeezed shut behind them and knocked a little crooked in ko.
  The neckwear is black and it is the one thing that varies: a floppy bow tie at the collar
  with a long necktie end hanging down the shirt front below it (idle, umbrella, shield,
  cheer, splash); in leap, run-l, run-r, dash-run and scared the long ends flap free,
  streaming back over his shoulder in run-l and run-r; in sit it reads as a plain loosened
  necktie; in eat there is no tie at all, only the open collar and the chain.
  Per-frame props, and nothing else ever: a white takeaway cup with a black lid and a brown
  sleeve hugged in both hands, a curl of steam off the lid, little jitter lines around him
  and small orange flame licks at his shoes (coffee); a whirling belt of gold coins circling
  his belly with a few more flying loose above him (magnet); a plain black umbrella with
  small brass rib tips and a curved wooden crook handle held up in one hand, the other hand
  on his hip (umbrella); a violet bubble crackling with lightning around his squat (shield);
  a red fry carton with one fry at his mouth and a fry crumb stuck on the shirt (eat); a
  small spray of pale water where his shoe and planted hand hit the ground (land); pale
  speed streaks behind him in dash-run and flee, with a spiky flame puff off the back shoe
  in dash-run; gold four-point sparkles around him (cheer); a ring of yellow stars (dizzy,
  ko); a burst of splash water with the whole suit soaked dark and the shirt gone
  see-through grey (splash). No magenta anywhere on him, his lenses or his nose, and none in
  the steam, streaks, bubble or splashes; the nose is always black.

HOW THIS BODY WORKS:
  A short, round, top-heavy little fellow about three heads tall: a big head, a barrel belly
  pushing at the shirt buttons, short arms and stubby legs. The head is the whole joke: a
  smooth bald skin-toned dome with a wrinkled forehead and heavy dark eyebrows, ringed by a
  shaggy fringe of black and brown raccoon fur that sticks out at the sides and back, round
  tan raccoon ears with pale rims, a black raccoon button nose, and plump tan furred jowls
  and chin. There is no full black eye mask; the dark fur runs from behind the glasses back
  to the ears. His hands are tan, fleshy and five-fingered. A bushy raccoon tail with dark
  brown and tan rings pokes out from under the jacket behind him in every frame except dizzy
  and ko (in shield it is only a dim shape behind him). He acts with the whole face: smug
  and half-lidded in idle, umbrella and shield, glum and droopy-lidded in sit, a sly
  sideways look in eat, a scowl in crouch, a closed-mouth grin in run-l and run-r, a big
  open laugh in leap, dash-run and cheer, bug-eyed in coffee, magnet, flee, scared and
  splash, tongue lolling in dizzy and ko. His height, belly, bald dome and glasses are
  identical in all 19, and the suit is always the same black jacket, white shirt and black
  trousers.
corrections: Tie claim was wrong. The block said the tie reads as a plain necktie in umbrella, but umbrella clearly shows the bow with the long end. The block also put the tie in ALL 19 FRAMES, but eat shows no tie at all, only the open collar and chain. I moved the tie out of the all-frames list and gave it its own per-frame line.

Expressions were wrong. Run-l and run-r are closed-mouth smug grins, not a big open laugh, so the laugh now covers leap, dash-run and cheer only. Sit is glum and droopy, not smug. Shield is smug and half-lidded, and crouch is a scowl.
Flee does not have both fists pumping: one hand is raised to his glasses. The stance now says so.
Idle has one hand raised to the glasses and the other on his hip. This was missing.

Added missing effects that the prop list ('nothing else ever') left out: the water spray at the shoe and planted hand in land, the speed streaks in dash-run and flee (plus the flame puff off the back shoe in dash-run), the gold sparkles in cheer and the jitter lines in coffee.
Coffee cup: added the black lid.
Magnet: added the coins flying loose above him.
Umbrella: added the brass rib tips.
Eat: the shirt carries one fry crumb, not 'a few crumbs'.
Ears: the sheet shows pale rims, not 'dark insides', so I changed that.
Tail: it is visible in every frame except dizzy and ko, so 'most frames' became that exact list.
Glasses: added that they are knocked crooked in scared. The arms read as dark tortoiseshell.
Shirt: it is cream-white with a chest pocket. Belt buckle: it reads as dull brass.
Dizzy is a belly-down sprawl with his face turned toward us, and ko shows the shoe soles. Leap and cheer arm poses added.
unsure: The steam in coffee, the speed streaks in dash-run and flee, and flecks in land, magnet and idle are pink or magenta on the reference, so I gave the steam no colour and forbade magenta.
Whether the dash-run burst at the back shoe is meant as a flame or as dust; it reads as a spiky pale flame puff.
The glasses arms look dark with orange mottling, which fits tortoiseshell, but they are too small to confirm the pattern.
The magnet whirl mixes round coins with a few bar-shaped pieces; these could be coins seen edge-on.
draftUnsure: Whether the black neckwear is one loose bow tie with long trailing ends or a bow tie worn over a separate necktie; it reads as a bow in most frames and as a plain necktie in sit and umbrella.
Whether the hands are bare skin or short tan fur; they read as fleshy tan with light texture.
The tail is not clearly visible in dizzy and ko (and only as a brown shape behind him in shield and splash), hence 'most frames'.

The run-l, run-r, dash-run and flee frames on the reference show a pink smudge at the front lens rim and nose, and the idle frame has pink specks at the hip and tail; I took these as cutout residue and forbade magenta rather than describing them.
Belt buckle metal colour (silver or brass) is too small to confirm.

mothman.block:
Mothman — one of the playable characters in Jimothy, a storybook hopper set on the rainy
streets of Seattle.

STANCE (locked — the same in every frame):
  Upright biped on two big clawed hind paws at rest (idle, coffee, magnet, umbrella,
  scared), arms hanging loose in idle and wings draped down his back like a cloak. He runs
  upright too: run-l, run-r, dash-run and flee are long bipedal strides, leaning forward
  with fists pumping and the wings folded flat behind him (in flee one paw clutches the side
  of his head by the goggles). Crouch is a low prowl with the forepaws dropped to the
  ground, one planted and one reaching ahead; leap is airborne with knees tucked, arms flung
  wide and wings open; land is a wide squat with both clawed hands spread and the wings
  raised. Scared stands knock-kneed with both paws clutched at his chest and the wings
  flared open. Cheer is a little hop, knees bent and toes pointed down, both arms thrown up
  and the wings spread. Shield is a tight huddle with the wings wrapped forward around him
  like a cocoon and both paws up at his mouth; sit is a round lump on his rump with the
  wings folded around him and the paws clasped on his belly; eat sits with the hind legs
  sprawled; dizzy is a belly-down sprawl on his flattened wings with his face turned to us;
  ko is on his back with the hind paws up.

WARDROBE AND PROPS (locked — these appear in ALL frames, including the deaths):
  No clothing at all. ALL 19 FRAMES: the goggles (two big round lenses in thick black rims,
  joined by a black bridge, with a black strap around his head; the lenses glow bright red
  with a white highlight), two long black bristly antennae rising from his crown, and his
  moth wings. The lenses only change to act: dimmed to dull red with sleepy half-lidded eyes
  showing through in umbrella and sit, red spirals in dizzy, dim with shut eyes in ko.
  Per-frame props, and nothing else ever: a cream takeaway cup with a lid and a brown sleeve
  held in both paws, a wisp of steam and orange flame licks around his feet (coffee); a
  whirl of crinkly gold bottle caps and golden fry sticks on streaking orange trails, with
  many of them stuck all over his fur and wings (magnet); a plain black umbrella speckled
  and dripping with rain, with a black crook handle, held up in one paw while the other
  rests on his belly (umbrella); a violet dome of honeycomb cells veined with crackling
  lightning (shield); one stray gold scrap stuck on his belly (scared); a red fry carton,
  one fry at his mouth and one fry resting on his chest ruff (eat); a spray of pale splash
  water under his feet (land); faint swoosh lines (leap); pale speed streaks behind him in
  dash-run and flee, with the wings smeared into a motion blur in dash-run; two small pale
  yellow zigzag shock marks over his head (flee); gold four-point sparkles around him
  (cheer); a ring of yellow stars (dizzy, ko); a burst of splash water with his fur soaked,
  plastered and dripping and the antennae drooping (splash). No magenta anywhere on him, and
  none in the steam, flames, trails, streaks or splashes.

HOW THIS BODY WORKS:
  A raccoon built like a moth: a stocky pear-shaped body covered head to toe in shaggy
  near-black fur with a plum-brown cast, and a pale mauve-grey fluffy ruff on the chest. The
  head is pure raccoon: rounded dark ears lined in tan, a dark mask edged by tan brow and
  cheek markings, a tan muzzle and a black nose, with the goggles sitting right over the
  mask. The wings make the silhouette: big dusky plum-brown moth wings with darker veins and
  a paler rim along the edges, each carrying a red ring eyespot with a dark centre. At rest
  they hang from his shoulders to his ankles like a cape with one eyespot showing low on
  each side; folded flat in the runs they show one or two eyespots on the near side; spread
  in leap, land and cheer each wing shows a big upper lobe with an eyespot near its tip;
  only in scared do they open fully into upper and lower lobes with an eyespot in each, four
  in all. A ringed raccoon tail, near-black with tan-grey rings, hangs behind him in most
  frames (hidden in dash-run, umbrella, shield, eat and splash). Hands and hind paws are big
  and dark with pale ivory claws, and a ragged fur cuff wraps each ankle like a worn-out leg
  warmer. The antennae are his mood meter: upright and curling when calm, swept back in the
  runs, stiff and straight up in scared, tied in a knot in dizzy, drooping and dripping in
  splash, one bent and one limp in ko. His face keeps a small closed smile at rest and in
  run-l and run-r, opens into a fanged grin in leap, magnet and cheer, yells in dash-run,
  flee, scared and splash, smirks sleepily in umbrella and sit, and hangs its tongue out in
  dizzy and ko. His size, pelt colour, goggles and wing pattern are identical in all 19; the
  wings never turn into bat wings or feathers.
corrections: Cheer is not an at-rest stand. It is a hop with bent knees and toes pointed down, arms up and wings spread. I took it out of the at-rest list and described it on its own.
Flee does not have both fists pumping: one paw clutches the side of his head by the goggles.

Spread wings: the block said leap, land, scared and cheer all show upper and lower lobes with an eyespot in each. Only scared shows four eyespots. Leap, land and cheer show one eyespot near the tip of each upper lobe.

The tail was listed in ALL 19 FRAMES, but it is hidden in dash-run, umbrella, shield, eat and splash. I moved it to the body section with that list. It does show in sit, which the writer thought was hidden.

Added missing effects: the water splash under his feet in land, the speed streaks in dash-run and flee (with the motion-blurred wings in dash-run), the gold sparkles in cheer and the swoosh lines in leap.
Magnet: the round pieces have crinkled edges like bottle caps, not flat coins. Described them as crinkly gold bottle caps and golden fry sticks on orange trails.
Umbrella: the crook handle is black and the canopy drips rain.
Shield: the dome has honeycomb cells, and both paws are held up at his mouth.
Scared: the small gold scrap stuck on his belly is clearly visible, so it is now listed. Added the scared pose too: knock-kneed, paws at his chest, wings flared.
Antennae: stiff and straight up in scared. In ko, one is bent and one is limp.
Added a short list of expressions per frame.
Wing edges: the sheet shows a paler rim, not a paler band.
unsure: Whether the gold scrap on his belly in scared is meant to be there or is left over from magnet. It is visible, so it is listed.
Whether the magnet sticks are fries or gold bars; they are blocky and golden-orange.
Cheer reads as a hop, but the feet sit at about the same height as in the standing frames.

The steam in coffee, the flames, the magnet trails and the dash-run and flee streaks lean pink or magenta, the land and splash water has purple tints, and one fingertip in eat has a pink fleck. Magenta is forbidden.
The goggle strap is clearly readable only in some frames.
draftUnsure: In scared there is a small gold object stuck on his belly (a stray fry or bottle cap left over from magnet?); I left it out of the prop list.
The goggle strap is only clearly readable in some frames (dizzy, ko, shield); in idle it is implied at the sides of the head.
In ko only one antenna reads clearly; the second may be bent out of view or broken.
In eat one fingertip shows a pink/magenta fleck, and the coffee flames and dash-run streaks lean pink; treated as effect or cutout colour, magenta forbidden.
The tail is hidden behind the wings in umbrella, shield and sit; 'all 19 frames' for the tail is by intent, not visible in every frame.
Whether the wings are two separate pairs or one pair with lobes is not fully clear; spread frames show an upper and a lower lobe on each side, each with an eyespot.

trashking.block:
The Trash King — one of the playable characters in Jimothy, a storybook hopper set on the
rainy streets of Seattle.

STANCE (locked — the same in every frame):
  Upright biped on bare raccoon hind paws, a stocky little monarch who stands wide and
  proud: idle is one fist on his hip with the spoon scepter planted beside him like a staff.
  The runs are low, forward-leaning bipedal bounds with the cape streaming behind: run-l and
  run-r with a fist pumping out front and the spoon held upright in the back paw, dash-run
  with the spoon carried level, flee with one paw clamping the crown to his head. Crouch is
  a low squat with the scepter planted in one paw and the other forepaw on the ground; leap
  is airborne with the scepter swung high, one knee tucked and the free arm flung out; land
  is a wide squat with the scepter spiked into the ground and the free arm flung out.
  Coffee, magnet, umbrella and cheer stand on both hind paws. Shield and scared hunch low
  with the paws at his chest; sit is on a small wooden seat with his legs apart; eat sits on
  the ground on his cape with his knees up and apart; dizzy is a face-down sprawl on his
  cape with the face turned to us; ko is on his back with his paws kicked up in the air.

WARDROBE AND PROPS (locked — these appear in ALL frames, including the deaths):
  ALL 19 FRAMES: a dented, tarnished brass crown (an open band with short spikes along the
  top edge and a row of small square rivets) worn tilted on his head; it pops off and hangs
  in the air above him in scared and sits crooked in dizzy and ko. A shaggy tan fur mantle
  round his shoulders freckled with dark spots, like a thrift-shop ermine. A tattered
  wine-red cape with a frayed, leaf-torn hem, flecked with gold specks, with a few tan
  square patches stitched on. A dented round tin lid scratched with a spiral, worn on his
  right shoulder as a pauldron (turned out of sight in leap, the four runs, cheer and
  splash). A cord of bronze beads carrying a round tarnished medallion with a scratched
  star-like mark (texture only, never a letter). A ragged patchwork tunic in olive green and
  rust brown with leaf-shaped patches and a jagged hem. A brown leather belt with a square
  brass buckle, hung all the way round with dangling junk: keys, little bottle-shaped
  charms, tags and red can rings.
  The scepter is a long, straight steel serving spoon about as tall as he is, the bowl
  chipped at the rim and crusted with brown-gold grime, with a banded metal collar just
  below the bowl. It is in play in 16 frames: planted as a staff in idle, crouch and land,
  gripped upright in run-l and run-r, carried level in dash-run, raised high in leap,
  magnet, cheer and splash, propped on his shoulder in coffee and eat, laid across his lap
  in sit, clutched to his chest in shield, lying on the ground under his paw in dizzy and
  lying across his body in ko. It is absent in flee, umbrella and scared.
  Per-frame props, and nothing else ever: a cream takeaway cup with a brown sleeve in both
  paws, little jitter flecks around him and orange flames licking at the cape hem (coffee);
  a whirl of gold bottle caps and orange fry sticks on streaking trails (magnet); a patched
  navy-purple umbrella with a stitched tan square patch, bottle caps stuck on the canopy and
  more dangling on strings from the rib tips, and a tan crook handle (umbrella); a violet
  hex-cell dome (shield); a stray bottle cap flying off with the crown (scared); a small
  brown wooden seat under him (sit); a red fry carton with a pale gold squiggle on the
  front, texture only, and one fry at his mouth (eat); gold bottle caps and gold four-point
  sparkles bursting around him (cheer); pale speed streaks behind him and a spiky pale gold
  burst at the back foot (dash-run, flee); a ring of yellow stars (dizzy, ko); a brown muck
  splash under his paws (land); a tall crown of splash water (splash). No magenta anywhere,
  including in the land splash, the magnet trails and the cheer sparkles.

HOW THIS BODY WORKS:
  A real raccoon under all the rags: stocky and short-legged, with dark grizzled brown fur,
  a bold black mask with cream brow bands and a cream muzzle, a black nose, long whiskers,
  rounded ears with pale rims, dark hands and bare dark hind paws with long toes. A ringed
  tail, dark brown and tan, peeks out from under the cape in run-l, run-r, flee, magnet,
  umbrella, cheer and ko; elsewhere the cape hides it. What makes him read is the pile:
  crown on top, spotted fur mantle, shoulder lid, medallion, patchwork tunic, the jangle of
  junk on the belt and the big spoon, all in a tarnished palette of brass, wine red, olive
  and rust. Everything is worn, dented and stained, never shiny new, never real gold. His
  face is regal and smug at rest (half-lidded in idle, sit and umbrella, a sly grin in
  crouch and land, a sly sideways look while eating) and cracks wide open in leap, dash-run,
  flee, magnet, cheer and splash, with bug eyes in coffee, magnet, flee, scared, cheer and
  splash and a nervous wide side-eye in shield. His size and the whole regalia are identical
  in all 19; the only piece allowed to leave his body is the crown, and only in scared, and
  the spoon sits out flee, umbrella and scared.
corrections: Spoon shape: it is straight, not 'slightly bent'. The collar below the bowl is banded, not wire-wrapped.
Eat is not seated 'the same way' as sit. No wooden seat shows; he sits on the ground on his cape with his knees up.
Umbrella: the sheet shows bottle caps stuck on the canopy and dangling on strings. There is no identifiable tag. The crook handle reads tan or brass, not clearly wood.
Tail: it also shows in umbrella, as a ringed tip at the lower left. Added it to the list.
Pauldron: it is not visible in leap, the four runs, cheer or splash. Added that note.
Flee: one paw clamps the crown to his head. The run poses are now spelled out, and leap has one knee tucked and the free arm flung out.

Added missing effects: the gold bottle caps and sparkles in cheer, the speed streaks and spiky burst at the back foot in dash-run and flee, the jitter flecks in coffee and the stray bottle cap in scared.
Whiskers: the writer called them white, but they read dark against the cream muzzle, so I removed the colour.
Expressions: coffee is bug-eyed with the mouth closed, not 'cracked wide open'. Leap and dash-run are open-mouthed, crouch and land show a sly grin, and shield is a nervous side-eye.
Final line: it now notes that the spoon is absent in flee, umbrella and scared, so it no longer conflicts with 'whole regalia identical in all 19'.
unsure: Whether a hidden seat is meant under him in eat; only cape and ground show.
In ko, the upper raised paw could be a forepaw or a second hind paw, so it is described only as paws kicked up.

chicken.block:
Chicken Suit Jimothy — one of the playable characters in Jimothy, a storybook hopper set on
the rainy streets of Seattle.

STANCE (locked — the same in every frame):
  Upright biped in the suit, standing on two yellow chicken feet at rest (idle, coffee,
  magnet, umbrella, scared, splash), one paw on his hip in idle. He runs upright in run-l,
  run-r and dash-run, leaning forward with fists pumping and big comic strides; flee faces
  LEFT like run-l, one paw clutching the top of the hood and the other wing-sleeve flapping
  out behind. Crouch is a low forward crouch with one paw planted on the ground; leap is an
  airborne seated tuck with both feet thrust forward, soles to the viewer, and both arms
  flung wide; land is a wide squat with both arms spread and the paws open. Shield is a
  lunging crouch with both paws up; scared is a knock-kneed cringe with both paws clutched
  under his chin; cheer is on one leg, the other knee kicked high and both arms up. Sit and
  eat are on his rump with both feet out front, soles showing, paws folded on the belly in
  sit; dizzy is a face-down sprawl with the head turned sideways; ko is on his back with
  both feet up in the air.

WARDROBE AND PROPS (locked — these appear in ALL frames, including the deaths):
  ALL 19 FRAMES: the full chicken onesie from hood to ankle, cream-white plush covered in
  scalloped feather texture. The hood has a bright yellow beak jutting forward over his brow
  like a cap brim, two small black bead eyes just above the beak, and a bright red comb on
  top (rounded lobes in idle, crouch, land, coffee, sit and eat; stretched back into
  streaming plumes in leap, run-l, run-r, dash-run and flee; flung straight up in scared).
  Two red teardrop wattles hang at his throat (flared out like a little red kerchief in
  run-l, run-r and dash-run). The arms are feathered wing-sleeves that fan into real feather
  fringes when he flaps (leap, dash-run, flee). A fan of cream-white tail feathers sticks
  out at his rump. His feet are yellow chicken-foot booties with three fat toes and brown
  claws. A small coral-red blush dot sits under the hood's bead eye in flee, umbrella,
  shield, cheer, dizzy, splash and ko.
  Per-frame props, and nothing else ever: a cream takeaway cup with a white lid and a brown
  sleeve in both paws, a wisp of steam, jitter lines and orange flames at his feet (coffee);
  gold bottle caps and orange fry sticks whirling round him, one cap stuck on his comb
  (magnet); a dark navy umbrella beaded with raindrops and dripping at the rim, with a black
  crook handle and a small red tip, and a gold bottle cap perched on his comb (umbrella); a
  violet hex-cell dome (shield); a red fry carton with one fry in his mouth and a second fry
  balanced on the beak (eat); a spray of pale splash water under his feet (land); pale speed
  streaks behind him in dash-run and flee, with a spiky pale gold burst off the back foot in
  dash-run; gold and pale blue four-point sparkles around him (cheer); a ring of yellow
  stars (dizzy, ko); a splash of water with the whole suit soaked, matted and dripping
  (splash). The hood is knocked askew with the beak tipped up in ko. No magenta anywhere,
  including the steam, the streaks and the land splash.

HOW THIS BODY WORKS:
  Jimothy inside a costume that is bigger than he is: the suit turns him into a round,
  pear-shaped ball of feathers with a neckless hood-head, stubby legs in the booties and
  arms swallowed by the wing-sleeves. Only three parts of the raccoon ever show. His face in
  the round hood opening: grey fur, black mask, white brows and muzzle, black nose, long
  whiskers, brown eyes. His dark brown five-fingered paws poking out of the sleeve cuffs.
  And his grey raccoon ears with pale rims, which stick out through the top corners of the
  hood in idle, crouch, leap, land, run-l, run-r, dash-run, coffee, sit and eat, and are
  hidden inside the hood in flee, magnet, umbrella, shield, scared, cheer, dizzy, splash and
  ko. No raccoon tail shows anywhere; his tail is the costume's feather fan. Cream suit,
  yellow beak and booties, red comb and wattles: that palette never shifts. The face does
  all the acting (smug and half-lidded in idle, sit and umbrella, a scowl in crouch and
  land, a whooping open grin in leap, dash-run, magnet and cheer, wide-eyed in coffee, flee,
  scared and splash, spiral eyes in dizzy, X eyes in ko) while the suit only flaps, flops
  and gets wet. His size and the suit's round mass are the same in all 19.
corrections: Flee: the block said fists pumping. On the sheet, flee faces left, one paw clutches the top of the hood and the other wing-sleeve flaps behind.
Scared comb: it is flung straight up, not stretched back. Land also shows the rounded comb. Added the scared pose too: knock-kneed, paws clutched under his chin.

Blush dots: the block listed only flee, umbrella and shield. They also appear in cheer, dizzy, splash and ko, always as a small dot under the hood's bead eye. I also changed their colour from pink to coral red.
Eat: added the second fry balanced on the hood's beak.

Added missing effects: the water splash under his feet in land, the speed streaks in dash-run and flee (with the spiky burst off the back foot in dash-run), and the gold and pale blue sparkles in cheer.
Coffee cup: added cream with a white lid. Umbrella: added that it drips at the rim.
Feather fringes: they show in flee as well as leap and dash-run.
Ears: they are grey with pale rims. Face: added the grey fur around the mask.
Expressions: sit is smug too, crouch and land are scowls, and leap, dash-run, magnet and cheer are open grins.
unsure: In splash, a darker grey-brown shape behind one leg reads as the soaked feather fan, not a raccoon tail.
Whether the gold bottle cap on the comb in magnet and umbrella is intended.
The coffee steam, the dash-run streaks, the land splash and flecks in idle and scared lean pink, magenta or purple on the reference; magenta is forbidden.
The red at the throat reads as two teardrop wattles, but in the runs it flares like a small kerchief.
draftUnsure: The raccoon ears show in some frames and not in others (listed in the block); the reference itself is inconsistent, so a repaint should follow the frame's own row.
In splash there is a darker grey-brown shape behind one leg that could be soaked tail feathers or a glimpse of a raccoon tail; I read it as soaked feathers.
The pink blush dots on the hood are faint and may be painting noise rather than a design detail.
Whether the red at the throat is meant as wattles or a small red bandana; it reads as two teardrop wattles in most frames and flares like a kerchief in the runs.
Whether the gold bottle cap on the comb in magnet and umbrella is intended or a stray from the magnet effect.

shinothy.block:
Shinothy — one of the playable characters in Jimothy, a storybook hopper set on the rainy
streets of Seattle.

STANCE (locked — the same in every frame):
  Upright biped with rock-star swagger, hip-shot on two sneakers, and one paw goes to his
  sunglasses at every chance (idle, crouch, land, flee, umbrella, sit); the free paw rests
  on his hip in idle, umbrella and cheer. He runs upright in run-l, run-r and dash-run, long
  bounding strides with fists up; flee faces LEFT, striding with one paw at his shades and
  the other fist back. Crouch is a deep squat with one paw touching the ground and the other
  tipping his shades; leap is airborne with one fist punched high, the other arm thrown out
  and the knees tucked; land is a wide squat with the free hand spread and sparks at both
  feet. Coffee is a wide-legged braced stance; magnet stands with one paw flung out and the
  other on his chest; shield is down on one knee with a palm raised; scared cringes
  knock-kneed with both paws at his chest; cheer stands with one fist punched high; sit
  reclines against his own tail with one knee up; eat sits cross-legged; dizzy is a
  belly-down sprawl with his face turned to us and the tail piled over his back; ko is on
  his back with both sneakers kicked up.

WARDROBE AND PROPS (locked — these appear in ALL frames, including the deaths):
  ALL 19 FRAMES: sunglasses with black rounded-rectangle lenses in black frames trimmed with
  gold, gold studs along the arms and a slanted gold glint bar across each lens. They sit on
  his nose, slid down so his eyes peek over the top in crouch, dash-run, flee, coffee,
  magnet, sit, eat and cheer, knocked crooked with the eyes staring out in scared, pushed up
  onto his forehead in dizzy and splash and knocked askew across his face in ko, but never
  lost. A black leather biker jacket with gold studs along the lapels and edges, gold zip
  and piping, silvery zigzag stitching on the sleeves and a small gold raccoon-face pin on
  the lapel. Teal-and-gold banded cuffs at both wrists. A black sparkly t-shirt with a thin
  gold chain and a small teal star pendant. A black gold-studded belt with a big spiky gold
  buckle shaped like a masked raccoon face. A heavy gold wallet chain swooping from the belt
  round to his back hip. Black jeans with a faint glitter. Black high-top sneakers covered
  in gold filigree, with a small gold raccoon-face badge at the ankle, white rubber soles
  and white toe caps. His hands are charcoal black, reading like black gloves, on grey
  furred forearms.
  Per-frame props, and nothing else ever: a cream takeaway cup with a white lid and a tan
  sleeve in both paws, a wisp of steam, jitter lines and orange flames at both sneakers
  (coffee); a whirl of gold bottle caps, gold sparkles and a flying red fry carton on gold
  ribbon trails circling him (magnet); an umbrella whose canopy matches his tail, glittering
  teal, silver and gold panels on gold ribs with a black underside and a gold shaft and tip
  (umbrella); a violet hex-cell dome (shield); a red fry carton with one fry at his mouth
  (eat); spiky pale gold sparks at both sneakers (land); speed streaks behind him in
  dash-run and flee, with a spark burst off the back sneaker in dash-run; two yellow zigzag
  shock marks (scared); gold four-point sparkles and a bright burst behind him (cheer); a
  ring of yellow stars (dizzy with thin orbit trails, ko); a burst of splash water (splash).
  No magenta anywhere, including rim light on the fur, the steam, the streaks and the bursts
  behind him.

HOW THIS BODY WORKS:
  Jimothy's build dressed to headline: a slim upright raccoon with a big head, pale
  silver-grey fur with a glitter sheen and white cheeks, a bold black mask, white brows,
  pale ears with dark insides and a spiky white tuft on the crown. The tail is the star:
  enormous, as big as his whole body, bushy and glittering like sequins, in broad bands of
  pearly silver-white and teal with a band or two of glittering gold (the band order shifts
  a little between frames). It curls up behind him at rest, arcs out behind him in the runs,
  serves as a cushion in sit, piles over his back in dizzy and frizzes out pale in scared.
  Everything he wears is black and gold, with teal only at the wrists and in the star
  pendant. The face plays it cool with a closed-mouth smirk in idle, run-l, run-r, sit and
  eat, flashes a toothy grin in crouch and land, opens into a grin in leap, dash-run, magnet
  and cheer, grits its teeth in shield, goes wide-eyed over the coffee cup, bug-eyed and
  open-mouthed in flee, scared and splash, and turns to green-and-white hypnotic ring eyes
  in dizzy and one X eye with the tongue out in ko. His size, shades, jacket, chains and
  tail pattern are identical in all 19.
corrections: Glasses, peeking eyes: leap does not show eyes above the lenses, so I removed it. Dash-run, flee, magnet and cheer do show eyes peeking over, so I added them.
Glasses, other frames: in scared they are knocked crooked with both eyes fully out, not slid down. In dizzy and splash they are pushed up onto his forehead, and in ko they sit askew across his face.
Glasses, frames: they read as black frames with gold trim and gold studs on the arms, not thin gold rims. The glint bars are slanted near-vertical bars.
Flee faces LEFT, with one paw at the shades and the other fist back. The block had flee in the list of upright runs with fists up.
Star pendant: it is teal with a gold outline on every frame where it can be read, not unconfirmed.
Belt buckle: it is a big spiky gold buckle shaped like a masked raccoon face.
Sneakers: removed the unconfirmable gold eyelets and added the gold raccoon-face badge at the ankle.
Jacket sleeves: the zigzag stitching reads silvery white, not gold.

Tail: the block said gold sits toward the tip, but the gold bands move around (near the base in idle and land, near the end in sit and ko). Now it says the band order shifts. It arcs behind him in run-l and run-r rather than trailing level.

Added missing effects: the speed streaks in dash-run and flee plus the spark burst off the back sneaker in dash-run, the jitter lines in coffee, the land sparks in the prop list and the gold sparkles in magnet.
Umbrella: added its black underside. Coffee cup: added the white lid.
Poses: magnet has one paw out and the other on his chest, scared has both paws at his chest, cheer has the free paw on his hip, and leap has the second arm thrown out.

Expressions: closed-mouth smirk in the idle, run-l, run-r, sit and eat frames; toothy grin in crouch and land; gritted teeth in shield. In coffee the mouth is hidden behind the cup, so only the wide eyes count there.
Fur: it is pale silver-grey with white cheeks.

Whether the teal-and-gold wrist bands are bangles or trim on the pushed-up jacket sleeves.
In land and umbrella an eye may faintly show above the lens, but it is too dim to confirm, so neither is in the peek list.
In splash the eyes read pale blue; I left eye colour out rather than lock it.
Coffee, magnet, cheer, dash-run, flee and splash have pink or magenta rim light, trails and bursts on the reference, and the fur tufts have pink edges in several frames; magenta is forbidden.
The shapes of the lapel pin, belt buckle and ankle badge are small; they read as masked raccoon faces and are described as ornament, not logos.

Whether the teal-and-gold wrist bands are bangles or trim on the jacket cuffs.
The exact order of the tail rings; silver-white and teal alternate with gold concentrated toward the tip, but the order shifts slightly between frames.
The shape of the belt buckle emblem and the lapel pin is too small to read beyond an ornate gold raccoon-like face; described as texture, not as a logo.

poses.inGame: standing, at rest — the default · on screen constantly
poses.pose: Standing four-square at rest on all four flat plantigrade paws, three-quarter to the camera and facing the viewer, weight settled and even, stubby ringed tail hanging low behind. Calm and content, chin a touch high, with a small closed-mouth smile. A few raindrops bead and drip off the fur, nothing is held in the paws, and nothing is painted beneath him.

poses.inGame: first quarter of every hop · 0.07s, hundreds of times a run
poses.pose: Flattened low on all fours and coiled to spring: haunches up, chest and shoulders down, elbows out, flat palms spread wide with heels down. Eyes locked forward on the next jump with a focused, ready look. Nothing is held in the paws, and nothing pools or casts a shadow between them.

poses.inGame: middle half of every hop · 0.15s, hundreds of times a run
poses.pose: Fully airborne, belly forward toward the viewer, forepaws flung out and up with flat palms open and hind legs trailing close beneath him, the spread kept compact enough that the frame stays roughly square. Mouth open in pure delight, eyes bright, stubby ringed tail short behind. A few flecks of rain shake off the fur and stay tight against the body, and nothing trails behind him.

poses.inGame: last quarter of a hop, plus a hold · 0.17s, hundreds of times a run
poses.pose: Touchdown: front paws slapped down flat with the fingers spread, body low and compressed as the weight is absorbed, whiskers pushed forward, head coming up with eyes wide. A small tight crown of splash bursts off the paws themselves, touching them and rising no higher than the knees. No puddle, pavement or cast shadow is painted beneath him.

poses.inGame: a sideways hop to the left · 0.28s
poses.pose: Side-on profile sprint to the left, snout leading toward the left edge of the frame: body low and long, legs at full extension through the stride, flat palms reaching forward and heels coming down, stubby ringed tail held short and level behind. Ears back and eyes fixed ahead on where he is landing, with at most a short spray of water flicking off the hind paws and touching them. Paint it facing left; do not mirror the right-facing frame, because straps and costume details must stay on their true sides.

poses.inGame: a sideways hop to the right · 0.28s
poses.pose: Side-on profile sprint to the right, snout leading toward the right edge of the frame: body low and long, legs at full extension through the stride, flat palms reaching forward and heels coming down, stubby ringed tail held short and level behind. Ears back and eyes fixed ahead on where he is landing, set and determined. At most a short spray of water flicks off the hind paws and stays touching them, with no long trail behind. Keep him facing right even if a reference painting faces the other way.

poses.inGame: the second stride of a sideways hop to the right, hero only · 0.28s
poses.pose: The second stride of the right-facing sideways sprint: the same side-on profile with the snout leading toward the right edge of the frame, and the same body height, head size and set, determined face as run-r. The limbs have swapped phase, so the forepaw that trailed now reaches out ahead of the snout while the other swings back behind the shoulder, and the hind leg that was tucked now stretches forward as the other pushes off behind. The stubby ringed tail stays short and level, so the two strides alternate cleanly without the body changing size.

poses.inGame: hopping while the coffee dash is up · 0.19s
poses.pose: Flat-out side-on sprint heading right like run-r but lower and longer, legs at maximum stretch, flat palms and heels reaching, ears pinned back and eyes wide. A few short warm speed streaks run close along the flanks and off the heels, stopping well inside the margin. No long trail, no rooster tail of water, and nothing painted beneath him.

poses.inGame: the street sweeper is closing in · seconds at a time
poses.pose: Panicked side-on sprint toward the left of the frame, flat out with the body low and legs at full stretch, flat palms and heels reaching, stubby tail short behind. Mouth wide open, eyes huge, ears pinned back as something closes in from behind. Short warm-red speed streaks stay tight behind the heels, and nothing tears loose or floats free of the body.

poses.inGame: STANDING STILL while the dash is up · 4.2s, or 7.0s on a Double Shot
poses.pose: Standing still, not running: reared up on both hind legs with heels planted flat, vibrating on the spot, both forepaws clamped around a takeaway coffee cup held at chest height with the face left clear. Pupils shrunk to pinpricks in enormous eyes, fur bristled out, short jitter lines doubling the outline. Pale cream steam curls off the cup and small warm fire licks flicker tight around his feet; the steam is never pink and the pose is never a run.

poses.inGame: standing while the Snacks magnet is up · 6.5s
poses.pose: Reared up on his hind legs, hugging an open paper fry carton to his belly with one forepaw while the other reaches out, mouth open and eyes shining with astonished delight that everything is coming to him. Gold bottlecaps and a few fries spiral in on a tight warm gold ribbon that overlaps his silhouette and stays within half a body width, with one or two already landed in the carton. The swirl stays warm gold and cream, never pink.

poses.inGame: standing while an umbrella shield is held · indefinite, until it takes a hit
poses.pose: Standing up on his hind legs, one forepaw gripping the handle of an open umbrella held close over his head, the canopy compact and only a little wider than his shoulders so it stays inside the cell. Rain drums on the canopy and sheds off its rim in short streaks that die in mid-air. Half-lidded eyes and a small, quietly smug closed-mouth smile, with no puddle, dry patch or ground beneath him.

poses.inGame: the instant the shield eats a hit · 0.55s
poses.pose: The instant of impact: braced low and flinching, forepaws thrown up in front of his face with flat palms out, eyes squeezed shut and muzzle scrunched. A bright blue-violet energy dome snaps up tight around his whole outline, no more than a hand's width out, with rain streaking and shattering off its outside curve. The dome stays blue-violet, never pink or magenta.

poses.inGame: a gull or crow is lining up a dive · 0.82 to 1.15s
poses.pose: Up on his hind legs and leaning back, both forepaws clutched tight to his chest, ears flat, head craned up and back. Eyes huge and white-rimmed, locked on something diving from above the frame, with a small worried open mouth. The bird itself is never painted; the threat stays off-frame.

poses.inGame: 4 seconds without input · until the player moves
poses.pose: The quiet frame: sitting up on his haunches, forepaws resting folded on his round belly, hind feet out in front and stubby tail tucked beside him. Half-lidded eyes gaze past the camera at the rain with a soft, content half-smile, a little alone. Calm and still, with a little rain on the fur and no puddle beneath him.

poses.inGame: 8 seconds without input · until the player moves
poses.pose: Sitting back on his haunches with an open paper fry carton hugged against his belly so it touches him, one forepaw lifting a single fry up to his mouth between flat fingers. Eyes on the fry, cheerfully absorbed and quietly delighted, a crumb or two caught in the fur. The carton stays against the body; nothing is set down, dropped or scattered below him.

poses.inGame: LEVEL CLEAR — the camera zooms in on them · 2.6s, the biggest moment in the game
poses.pose: Standing tall on his hind legs with heels down and chest out, one forepaw punched up toward the sky with the arm bent so the paw stays close above his head, mouth wide open in a whoop of pure joy, ears up. A small burst of warm gold sparks and confetti hangs tight around his shoulders and overlaps his outline. Keep the whole pose compact, because this frame is shown biggest under the zoom and a tall stretch shrinks him.

poses.inGame: death by the street sweeper · 1.55s, same treatment
poses.pose: Sprawled and spun out, slumped back on his haunches and tipping over onto one side, limbs gone loose. Spiral eyes, tongue lolling out, ears and whiskers knocked askew in a woozy wobble. The large, clear spiral eyes are what set this death apart from ko; funny-sad, never grim, and nothing painted beneath him.

poses.inGame: death by water · 1.55s, same treatment
poses.pose: The instant of the burst: soaked to the skin with fur plastered flat and dark, both arms thrown straight up with flat palms spread, eyes wide and mouth open in betrayed shock. A tight crown of pale blue-white water explodes up around his middle so his body stays centred in it, the spray touching him and never reaching a cell edge. He is not sinking or going under, and no flat pool, ripple rings or ground are painted.

poses.inGame: death by traffic, gull or steam · 1.55s, camera leans in, light closes
poses.pose: Flat on his back with the body laid on a slight diagonal so the frame stays near square, all four legs in the air with flat palms and pads turned up, stubby tail pressed beneath him. Dazed, swooning half-moon lids, tongue lolling out one side, and a small ring of gold stars circling close around his head. Funny-sad, never grim: under the daze he looks quietly relieved to finally be lying down, with nothing painted beneath him.
